docs.title: ACE3P Documentation
docs.text:
ACE3P (Advanced Computational Electromagnetic 3D Parallel) is a suite of parallel finite-element codes developed at SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory for the design and analysis of particle accelerator components. It solves Maxwell's equations and coupled multiphysics problems on unstructured tetrahedral meshes with high-order basis functions, and runs on HPC systems using MPI.

  • Getting started

    Set up your environment on S3DF or NERSC Perlmutter, install Cubit and ParaView locally, and run your first job.

    Getting started

  • Workflow

    The common ACE3P pipeline: geometry and meshing in Cubit, mesh conversion with acdtool, solving, and post-processing.

    Workflow overview

  • Modules

    User guides and tutorials for each solver: Omega3P, S3P, T3P, Track3P, Pic3P, TEM3P, and Gun3P.

    Module guides

  • Reference

    Input-file keyword tables generated directly from the ACE3P source, so they always match the released code.

    Keyword reference

docs.title: Solver modules
docs.text: Module Domain Typical use Omega3P Frequency domain, eigenmodes Cavity resonant modes, Q factors, R/Q, mode damping with couplers S3P Frequency domain, driven S-parameters of couplers, waveguides, and multi-port structures T3P Time domain Wakefields, transient response, beam-driven fields Track3P Particle tracking Multipacting, dark current, field emission Pic3P Particle-in-cell Self-consistent beam dynamics with space charge TEM3P Multiphysics Thermal and mechanical analysis coupled to RF fields Gun3P Electrostatic / beam optics Electron guns, space-charge-limited emission acdtool Utility Mesh conversion and statistics, RF post-processing, field extraction

docs.title: About these docs
docs.text:
This site replaces the CW23 workshop slide decks that were distributed as PDFs. The content is organized as a manual rather than as lecture notes, it is searchable, and it is versioned alongside ACE3P releases. Use the version selector in the header to view documentation for a specific release.

The keyword reference pages are regenerated from the ACE3P source tree whenever a release is tagged. See Contributing for how that works and how to propose changes.

Citing ACE3P

Please cite ACE3P when publishing results obtained with it. Contact the development team at ace3p@slac.stanford.edu.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: This documentation is maintained in the slaclab/ace3p-docs repository. Readers can file issues; changes go through pull requests.

docs.title: Report a problem
docs.text: Use the Edit this page icon at the top of any page to open the source on GitHub, or open an issue at https://github.com/slaclab/ace3p-docs/issues. Include the page URL and, for technical errors, the ACE3P version you observed the behavior with.

docs.title: Build locally
docs.text:
git clone git@github.com:slaclab/ace3p-docs.git
cd ace3p-docs
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
mkdocs serve

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000. The site rebuilds on every save. Run mkdocs build --strict before pushing; it fails on broken links and missing pages, which is also what continuous integration checks.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
docs/
  index.md              home page
  getting-started/      system setup: S3DF, Perlmutter, local tools
  workflow/             the common pipeline: input format, mesh, batch jobs
  modules/              one guide per solver; omega3p/ has tutorials
  reference/            GENERATED keyword tables, do not edit by hand
  interfaces/           GUI, dashboard, workflow assistant
  assets/               images, grouped by module
tools/
  extract_keywords.py   generates docs/reference/*.md from ACE3P source
mkdocs.yml              navigation and theme

Add a new page by creating the Markdown file and adding it to nav in mkdocs.yml.

docs.title: Writing guidelines
docs.text:
• Write prose, not slide bullets. Each tutorial step says what to do, what to expect, and why.
  • Show real input files from the examples directory, complete and runnable. Annotate with comments rather than paraphrasing.
  • Use system-neutral commands in module guides. Put S3DF and Perlmutter specifics in Getting Started.
  • Images go in docs/assets/<module>/ and are referenced with relative paths.
  • Do not commit credentials, personal home-directory paths, or unpublished results.

docs.title: Regenerating the reference pages
docs.text:
The reference tables come from the ACE3P source tree:

python tools/extract_keywords.py /path/to/ace3p --out docs/reference --modules omega3p emfem solver

The script scans for Get(kvc, "Keyword", InitOrFallback<T>(default) ...) and find("Keyword") calls. When the ACE3P source repository tags a release, a continuous-integration job there will run this script and open a pull request here with the updated pages. Until that job exists, run the script by hand before tagging a documentation version.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
Documentation versions are published with mike. Pushing to main updates the dev version. Pushing a tag vX.Y publishes that version and points the latest alias at it:

git tag v2026.10
git push origin v2026.10

Tag the documentation with the same version string as the ACE3P release it describes.

docs.title: Corrections to source material
docs.text:
This documentation was converted from the CW18 and CW23 workshop slide decks and grounded in the example directories that ship with them. The slides, the example files, and the stored results do not always agree with each other, and some of the stored results no longer match what the current ACE3P build produces. This page records every such discrepancy found during conversion, what the documentation says instead, and why.

Keep adding to this list. When a reader reports that a value in the docs does not match what they see, check here first; if it is a new case, add it.

docs.title: Conventions used in this documentation
docs.text:
• The example file on disk wins over the slide. When the slide listing and the file in examples/ differ, the docs show the file, because that is what a user will run.
  • Stored results are quoted as stored, with their build date. When a tutorial quotes a number from an omega3p.out or track3p_results/ in the example directory, that number came from whichever ACE3P build produced the stored file, which may be a decade old.
  • Reruns on current builds are labelled as such. Where the same input has been rerun recently, both results are shown and the difference is discussed rather than hidden.
  • No numbers are invented. Where an earlier draft of these pages contained an illustrative value that did not come from a file, it has been replaced with the real value or removed. Those cases are listed below under "Errors in earlier drafts of this documentation".

docs.text: Item Note Hybrid MPI and OpenMP The slides predate OpenMP support in Track3P. docs.text: Source deck: T3P-Tutorial.pptx (CW23, March 2023). Stored results were produced with the March 2023 ACE3P build, so unlike Track3P there is no build-age gap between slides and results. docs.title: Element counts
docs.text:
The acdtool statistics shown on the slides were captured from meshes that differ from the .ncdf files now in the example directories. The documentation quotes the count from t3p.log of the stored run.

Example Slide acdtool listing Stored mesh and t3p.log cavity-quarter 8,537 7,552 cavity-half 17,703 15,516 BPM 68,326 68,720 taper 9,795 8,536

The stored acdtool.log in each directory agrees with t3p.log, so the slides were made from an earlier mesh. Loss and kick factors in the docs are from the stored wakefield.out and therefore correspond to the stored meshes.

The CW23 Track3P deck (Track3P-Tutorial.pdf, 144 pages) extends the CW18 version (134 pages) used for the original Track3P pages. A page-title diff found the additions, which are now in the Track3P pages:

docs.title: Omega3P additions from the CW23 deck
docs.text: The CW23 Omega3P deck is 76 pages against the CW18 version's 84; practices 3b and 4 were condensed into two slides, "Important TIPs" and "Non-linear Eigensolver Parameters". The TIPs slide adds guidance not in the CW18 deck: a multi-port problem is quadratic (and solvable without CORK) when every port has one mode and all ports share the same cutoff; otherwise use the 1D absorbing boundary as an approximation, PML as a better approximation, or CORK for accuracy. The CORK example gains an OneRKSShift: 1 key not present in the CW18 deck or the example files. These points are now in the Omega3P module page (tip box in the input section) and in the Omega3P command syntax page, where OneRKSShift was confirmed to be read by solver/src/CORK_RationalNewton.C.

docs.title: Errors in earlier drafts of this documentation
docs.text:
These were introduced during conversion and fixed on 2026-10-19 after a verification pass against the example directories.

  1. Omega3P Tutorial 2, coax coupler. The first draft contained a mode summary with Qext 4100 and Q0 28,500 that was written as an illustration, not taken from a file. Replaced with the stored result, Qext 1,024,236. The difference is more than two orders of magnitude and would have misled anyone using the example to check their installation.
  2. Omega3P Tutorial 1, convergence study. Stated the mesh journals went from fine to coarse as mesh0 to mesh3; the opposite is true.
  3. Omega3P Tutorial 1, Q0. Quoted as "about 28,900"; the stored value is 28,885.
  4. Omega3P post-processing page, R/Q convention. The note stating acdtool uses the circuit convention V²/(ωU) per cavity was inferred from the output header comment RoverQ=V^2/(omega*U) and not independently confirmed in source. It remains in the docs but is flagged here as unverified against code.
  5. Module index. S3P, Track3P, and T3P were listed as outline stubs after their guides were written. Fixed when each guide landed.
  6. T3P tutorials, element counts. The first draft quoted the slide acdtool counts (8,537; 17,703; 68,326; 9,795). Replaced with the stored-mesh counts from t3p.log on 2026-10-19 before publication.
  7. T3P tutorials, BPM solver. The first draft said the misspelled Slover key made T3P use "the default" without naming it. Traced in NML_ITLLinearSolver.C: the default is the best direct solver compiled in, MUMPS on these builds.
  8. T3P tutorials, SIBC power. The first draft said "roughly 40%" transmitted from eyeballing the plot. Replaced with 46% from integrating the monitor files.
  9. TEM3P module page, LF pressure. First draft gave the pressure formula without its sign convention. Checked LFDetuning.C: pressure is \(\tfrac{1}{4}(\mu_0 H^2 - \varepsilon_0 E^2)\) and the load vector is scaled by −1 times the outward normal, so a positive (magnetic-dominated) pressure pushes the wall outward from the vacuum, which is inward on the metal. Wording adjusted.
  10. Getting Started, example paths. The first draft pointed at the personal copy /sdf/data/rfar/nfs/acd/u01/userspace/cho/cw23/, which lacks Gun3P and the CW23 Track3P additions. Changed to the group copy /sdf/group/rfar/ace3p/cw23/ on 2026-10-19 when the difference was discovered.
  11. This page, Track3P section. The first draft flagged the slide's Omega3P mode 2 frequency of 1.75 GHz as suspicious. It is correct; the stored output confirms it, and the physics (a dipole mode visible only in the full model) explains it. The entry now says so.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
ACE3P runs on HPC systems. Pre- and post-processing happen on your own computer with Cubit and ParaView, while the solvers run on a cluster through the Slurm batch scheduler.

flowchart LR
    subgraph Laptop
        A[Cubit<br/>geometry + mesh] 
        E[ParaView<br/>visualization]
    end
    subgraph HPC["HPC system (S3DF or Perlmutter)"]
        B[acdtool meshconvert]
        C[Solver<br/>omega3p, s3p, ...]
        D[acdtool postprocess]
    end
    A -- "scp .gen" --> B --> C --> D
    C -- "scp .mod" --> E

Choose the system you will run on:

  • S3DF, SLAC's Shared Scientific Data Facility. Use this if you are at SLAC or have an S3DF account.
  • NERSC Perlmutter. Use this if you have access to the m349 ACE3P allocation at NERSC.

Then install the local tools on your laptop and continue to the workflow overview.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• An account on S3DF or NERSC with access to the ACE3P installation.
  • Familiarity with a Unix shell: cd, ls, cp, mkdir, and a text editor such as vi, emacs, or nano.
  • An SSH client. Linux and macOS have ssh and scp built in. On Windows 10 or later, use ssh from PowerShell, or install PuTTY and WinSCP.

docs.title: Example files
docs.text:
The tutorials in this documentation use the examples and exercises prepared for the CW23 workshop. They are available on both systems:

System Examples Exercises S3DF /sdf/group/rfar/ace3p/cw23/examples /sdf/group/rfar/ace3p/cw23/exercises Perlmutter $CFS/ace3p/cw23/examples $CFS/ace3p/cw23/exercises

The S3DF copy under /sdf/group/rfar/ace3p/cw23/ is the current one and also holds the per-module command references in commands/, the ParaView macros in macros/, and release notes in news/. An older personal copy at /sdf/data/rfar/nfs/acd/u01/userspace/cho/cw23/ lacks the Gun3P example and the CW23 Track3P additions.

Copy the directory you need into your own working area before running anything, since the example directories are read-only for most users.

docs.title: Local tools: Cubit and ParaView
docs.text: Geometry, meshing, and visualization run on your own computer.

docs.title: Cubit
docs.text:
Cubit from Sandia National Laboratories is the geometry and meshing tool used throughout the ACE3P workflow. It requires a license. The tutorials were written with Cubit 16.x.

ACE3P uses Cubit through journal files (.jou), which are scripts of Cubit commands. Two ways to run one:

  1. Click the Play button in the toolbar, browse to the .jou file, and open it.
  2. Open Tools, then Journal Editor, load the file, and press Play. The editor lets you step through and modify commands.

A full walkthrough of building and meshing a cavity is on the Cubit page. The export command that ACE3P needs is Genesis format with all blocks:

export Genesis "model4.gen" block all overwrite

Mesh elements must be quadratic tetrahedra (tetra10) and the model must be scaled to meters before export. See Mesh preparation.

docs.title: Cubit on S3DF
docs.text:
A licensed Cubit is installed at /sdf/group/rfar/software/Cubit-16.12/. Use it through a NoMachine remote desktop, through ssh -X, or in batch mode without a GUI:

/sdf/group/rfar/software/Cubit-16.12/cubit -batch -nographics -input step2-Mesh-pillbox.jou

docs.title: ParaView
docs.text: ParaView is free. Install version 5.11 or later to match the SLAC plugin.

docs.title: Enable the SLAC toolbar
docs.text:
1. Open Tools, then Manage Plugins.
  2. Select SLACTools and click Load Selected.
  3. Expand the entry and check Auto Load so it is active on every start.

The SLAC toolbar adds a reader that loads an ACE3P mesh (.ncdf) together with mode or field files (.mod) in one step.

docs.title: Load the ACE3P macros
docs.text:
The CW23 materials include Python macros for common ACE3P plots. Add each one through Macros, then Add new macro:

Macro Used with Purpose nextmode.py Omega3P, S3P, T3P, TEM3P Step through modes or time steps enhancement.py Track3P Plot the enhancement counter resonant.py Track3P Plot resonant particles trajectory.py Track3P Animate particle trajectories wakeplot.py T3P Plot wake potentials timeFFT.py T3P FFT of a time signal

The macros are in the macros/ directory alongside the examples.

docs.title: ParaView on S3DF
docs.text: A ParaView 5.11.1 build with web components is installed at /sdf/group/rfar/software/ParaView-5.11.1-MPI-Linux-Python3.9-x86_64/. It can serve the ParaView Web Visualizer so you can look at results in a browser through an SSH tunnel without copying files to your laptop. See Web dashboard.

docs.title: Running on NERSC Perlmutter
docs.text: Perlmutter is NERSC's flagship system. ACE3P is installed in the ace3p project directory on the Community File System (CFS) and currently runs on the CPU nodes. Each CPU node has two AMD EPYC 7763 processors, 128 cores in total, and 512 GB of memory.

docs.title: Log in
docs.text:
ssh <username>@perlmutter.nersc.gov

Enter your password followed immediately by your six-digit one-time password, with no space between them.

docs.title: Avoid repeated OTP prompts with sshproxy
docs.text:
NERSC provides sshproxy to generate a key that is valid for 24 hours.

Linux and macOSWindows 
scp <username>@dtn01.nersc.gov:/global/cfs/cdirs/mfa/NERSC-MFA/sshproxy.sh .
./sshproxy.sh -u <username>
ssh -l <username> -i ~/.ssh/nersc perlmutter.nersc.gov

scp <username>@dtn01.nersc.gov:/global/cfs/cdirs/mfa/NERSC-MFA/sshproxy.exe .
.\sshproxy.exe -u <username> --format openssh -o nersc
ssh -l <username> -i nersc perlmutter.nersc.gov

For PuTTY or WinSCP, omit --format openssh to get a .ppk key.

docs.title: Load the ACE3P environment
docs.text:
cp $CFS/ace3p/perlmutter/CPU/perlmutter-ace3p.sh ~/
source ~/perlmutter-ace3p.sh

The ACE3P binaries live in $CFS/ace3p/perlmutter/CPU/. $CFS expands to /global/cfs/cdirs.

docs.title: Working directory
docs.text:
Run jobs from scratch, not from your home directory:

mkdir -p $SCRATCH/ace3p
ln -s $SCRATCH/ace3p ~/ace3p
cd ~/ace3p

docs.title: Transfer files
docs.text:
Use the data transfer nodes dtn01 through dtn04:

# laptop -> Perlmutter
scp pillbox4.gen <username>@dtn01.nersc.gov:ace3p/pillbox/
# Perlmutter -> laptop
scp '<username>@dtn01.nersc.gov:ace3p/pillbox/omega3p_results/*.mod' .

Windows users can do the same in WinSCP with protocol SCP, host dtn01.nersc.gov, port 22.

docs.title: A minimal batch script
docs.text:
run-omega3p.batch
#!/bin/bash -l
#SBATCH -C cpu
#SBATCH -q debug
#SBATCH -A m349
#SBATCH -N 1
#SBATCH -t 00:10:00
#SBATCH -J omega3p
#SBATCH -e ace3p.e%j
#SBATCH -o ace3p.o%j

srun -n 16 -c 16 --cpu-bind=cores $CFS/ace3p/perlmutter/CPU/omega3p pillbox.omega3p
Line Meaning -C cpu Request CPU nodes -q debug Short test queue, 30 minute limit. Use regular for production. -A m349 The ACE3P allocation -n 16 -c 16 16 MPI ranks, 16 cores each, filling one 128-core node 
sbatch run-omega3p.batch
squeue -u $USER       # or: sqs
scancel <jobid>
tail -f ace3p.o<jobid>

See the NERSC job documentation for queue policies and more options.

docs.title: Running on S3DF
docs.text: S3DF is SLAC's Shared Scientific Data Facility. ACE3P is installed under the rfar group area and runs on the milano partition.

docs.title: Log in
docs.text:
ssh <username>@s3dflogin.slac.stanford.edu

Login nodes are for editing and job submission only. Do not run solvers on them.

docs.title: Load the ACE3P environment
docs.text:
Source the environment script once per session. It loads the matching OpenMPI module and puts the ACE3P binaries on your PATH.

source /sdf/group/rfar/ace3p/ace3p.sh
which omega3p acdtool

Tip

Add the source line to your ~/.bashrc if you use ACE3P regularly.

docs.title: Partitions and accounts
docs.text:
Setting Value Notes Partition milano AMD Milan nodes, 128 cores per node Account rfar:regular Replace rfar with your own allocation if different QOS normal Non-preemptable; use preemptable for lower-priority throughput

Check your allocations with sacctmgr show assoc user=$USER format=account,partition,qos.

docs.title: A minimal batch script
docs.text:
run-omega3p.sh
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --partition=milano
#SBATCH --account=rfar:regular
#SBATCH --qos=normal
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=16
#SBATCH --time=00:30:00
#SBATCH --job-name=omega3p
#SBATCH --output=%x.%j.out
#SBATCH --error=%x.%j.err

source /sdf/group/rfar/ace3p/ace3p.sh
srun --overlap --cpu-bind=none -n 16 omega3p pillbox.omega3p

Submit, monitor, and cancel with the usual Slurm commands:

sbatch run-omega3p.sh
squeue -u $USER
scancel <jobid>

docs.title: Interactive sessions
docs.text:
For short tests, allocate an interactive shell on a compute node:

srun --partition=milano --account=rfar:regular -n 16 --time=01:00:00 --pty /bin/bash
source /sdf/group/rfar/ace3p/ace3p.sh
mpirun -n 16 omega3p pillbox.omega3p

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
Location Use $HOME Scripts and small inputs. Quota is limited. /sdf/group/rfar/<user> Project space for inputs and results. /sdf/scratch/<group>/<user> Large temporary output. Purged periodically.

Temporary files

Some ACE3P tools write scratch files to $TMPDIR. If /lscratch on a node is full, set export TMPDIR=/sdf/scratch/<group>/<user>/tmp before running.

docs.title: Hybrid MPI and OpenMP
docs.text:
Track3P and some T3P workloads benefit from hybrid execution. Request one MPI rank per socket and let OpenMP fill the cores:

export OMP_NUM_THREADS=16
srun -n 1 -c 16 track3p input.track3p

See the module guides for solver-specific recommendations.

docs.title: Interfaces
docs.text:
The command line is the primary way to run ACE3P, and everything in this documentation can be done from a terminal. Three higher-level interfaces are being developed around the same solvers and input files.

Interface What it does Where it runs Status ACE3P GUI Desktop application for building input files and launching jobs Perlmutter (Linux), Windows First release, v1.4.15 Web dashboard Browser-based input generators, workflow documentation, job monitoring S3DF, via SSH tunnel Prototype AI workflow assistant Natural-language generation of multi-step workflow specifications, executed by Maestro on Slurm S3DF Prototype, validated on Omega3P and Track3P

All three produce the same .omega3p, .s3p, and other input files described in this manual, and all three submit the same solver binaries. Learning the input format here carries over to any of them.

Two further Python toolkits drive ACE3P programmatically and are not yet documented here:

  • lume-ace3p, public on GitHub, wraps Cubit, acdtool, and the ACE3P solvers in the LUME interface for design parameter scans.
  • A3PI, the ACE3P-IMPACT integration, chains Cubit, Omega3P, acdtool field extraction, and the IMPACT-T beam dynamics code under libEnsemble for gun optimization. Its user guide and an example are in the commands/ and examples/a3pi/ directories of the CW23 materials.

docs.title: Web dashboard
docs.text:
The ACE3P Workflow Dashboard is a browser application that documents the simulation workflow, generates solver input files from forms, produces Slurm scripts, and monitors running workflows.

Source: https://github.com/lge0303/ace3p-dashboard

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
Area Pages Input generators Omega3P, S3P, T3P, Track3P, TEM3P. Fill in boundary conditions and solver parameters in a form, preview the generated file, download it. Slurm script generator Omega3P batch scripts for Perlmutter and S3DF Post-processing .rfpost file generator for acdtool postprocess rf Workflow monitor Live status of Maestro workflows, reading Slurm squeue and Maestro output directories, refreshed every few seconds AI generator Front end for the workflow assistant

The dashboard is built with Next.js and runs on S3DF. Users reach it through an SSH tunnel:

ssh -L 3000:localhost:3000 <username>@s3dflogin.slac.stanford.edu
# then open http://localhost:3000

No data leaves S3DF. Form logic runs in the browser and generated files are downloaded locally.

docs.title: Visualization in the browser
docs.text:
ParaView 5.11 on S3DF includes the ParaView Web Visualizer, which renders 3D data server-side and streams it to a browser:

PVDIR=/sdf/group/rfar/software/ParaView-5.11.1-MPI-Linux-Python3.9-x86_64
$PVDIR/bin/pvpython $PVDIR/share/paraview-5.11/web/visualizer/server/pvw-visualizer.py \
  --data /path/to/omega3p_results --port 8080

Tunnel port 8080 and open http://localhost:8080. This avoids copying large .mod files to a laptop. Integrating the visualizer into the dashboard is planned.

docs.title: ACE3P GUI
docs.text: The ACE3P GUI is a desktop application for preparing input files and launching ACE3P jobs without editing text files by hand. Its first release is version 1.4.15.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text:
Perlmutter (Linux)Windows

The compiled executable is installed in the ACE3P project directory:

/global/cfs/cdirs/ace3p/gui/ACE3P-GUI-v1.4.15-linux-x86_64/ACE3P-GUI

Connect to Perlmutter through ThinLinc so that a graphical desktop is available, open a terminal, and launch the executable from it.

A Windows build is distributed through SLAC SharePoint. Ask the ACE3P team for the current download link.

docs.title: Documentation status
docs.text:
Under construction

A user guide for the GUI has not been written yet. This page will cover the main windows, how a GUI session maps onto the .omega3p and other input files described in this manual, and how to submit and monitor jobs from the GUI. Feedback on the first release should go to the ACE3P team.

docs.title: AI workflow assistant
docs.text:
Multi-step ACE3P campaigns, such as a mesh convergence study, a gradient sweep for multipacting, or an Omega3P-to-Track3P pipeline, involve many Slurm jobs with dependencies between them. The S3DF workflow project automates these with the Maestro workflow engine and uses an AI assistant to generate the workflow specification from a plain-English description.

Source: https://github.com/lge0303/s3df-workflow

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    U["User: 'Sweep gradient 10 to 50 MV/m<br/>in Track3P for pillbox cavity'"] --> A["AI assistant<br/>knows ACE3P inputs,<br/>S3DF Slurm settings"]
    A --> Y["Maestro YAML<br/>steps + dependencies + sweep"]
    Y --> M["maestro run"]
    M --> S["Slurm jobs:<br/>meshconvert, omega3p,<br/>track3p x N, analyze"]
    S --> R["Plots and summary"]

The assistant does not replace the workflow engine or the scheduler. It writes the specification; Maestro resolves dependencies and submits jobs; Slurm runs them. The user reviews the generated YAML before anything is submitted.

docs.title: Validated pipelines
docs.text:
Workflow What it does Result Omega3P single solve Pillbox cavity, 16 MPI ranks Mode 1 at 1.3138 GHz, matches reference to 8 digits FE order convergence Three parallel Omega3P runs, orders 1 to 3, with a fan-in comparison step Order 1 has 0.08% error; order 2 converged Omega3P to Track3P Eigenmode solve, then multipacting scan over field levels, then plot generation Resonant particles and enhancement counter at 23 to 25 MV/m

The whole Omega3P-to-Track3P pipeline runs in about five minutes on the S3DF milano partition.

docs.title: Example specification
docs.text:
A generated Maestro step for the solver looks like this:

- name: omega3p-solve
  description: Run Omega3P eigenmode solver
  run:
    cmd: |
      source /sdf/group/rfar/ace3p/ace3p.sh
      cd $(WORKSPACE)
      srun --overlap --cpu-bind=none -n 16 omega3p pillbox.omega3p
    depends: [meshconvert]
    nodes: 1
    procs: 16
    walltime: "00:30:00"

Parameter sweeps use Maestro's global.parameters block, which expands one step into one job per value. Fan-in steps that aggregate results depend on step_*.

docs.title: Relationship to this documentation
docs.text: The assistant's knowledge of ACE3P input files comes from the same information presented in this manual. As the keyword reference is generated from source, it becomes a reliable foundation for validating generated inputs. Keeping the documentation and the workflow tooling in step is a goal of both projects.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
ACE3P is a family of solvers that share one mesh format, one input syntax, and one post-processing toolchain. Each module addresses a different physics regime.

Module Guide Status of this documentation Omega3P User guide and tutorials Complete: concepts, three tutorials, post-processing S3P User guide and tutorials Complete: concepts, input blocks, output files, three tutorials T3P User guide and tutorials Complete: wakefields, port excitation, moving window, SIBC, five tutorials Track3P User guide and tutorials Complete: multipacting and dark current, six tutorials, S3DF rerun Pic3P User guide and tutorial Complete: self-consistent PIC, LCLS gun tutorial TEM3P User guide and tutorials Complete: thermal, elastic, LF detuning, mechanical eigenmodes, four tutorials Gun3P User guide and tutorial Complete: DC gun iteration, sheet beam gun tutorial with MICHELLE comparison

docs.title: Which module do I need?
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Q1{What do you want?} 
    Q1 -->|Resonant frequencies, Q, R/Q, field patterns| O[Omega3P]
    Q1 -->|Transmission and reflection vs frequency| S[S3P]
    Q1 -->|Wakefields or transient beam-driven fields| T[T3P]
    Q1 -->|Multipacting or dark current| TR[Track3P]
    Q1 -->|Self-consistent beam with space charge| P[Pic3P]
    Q1 -->|Heating, stress, or frequency shift from deformation| TE[TEM3P]
    Q1 -->|Electron gun or DC beam optics| G[Gun3P]

Several modules chain together. Track3P reads the mode fields that Omega3P produces. TEM3P reads Omega3P or S3P fields as a heat source. The workflow assistant page shows how such chains are automated.

docs.title: Gun3P
docs.text: Gun3P is a static solver for DC electron guns. It computes the electrostatic potential from the electrode voltages, emits electrons from the cathode under the space-charge limit, tracks them, deposits their charge, and iterates until the fields and the beam are self-consistent. Optionally it also solves the magnetostatic field of the beam's own current. The outputs are the emitted current, the beam trajectories and envelope, emittances at a screen, and the fields on the mesh.

docs.title: What it solves
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    I["Initialize"] --> E["Electrostatic solve<br/>∇·(ε∇φ) = −ρ"]
    E --> M["Magnetostatic solve<br/>∇×(μ⁻¹∇×A) = J<br/>(optional)"]
    M --> T["Emit at cathode,<br/>track particles,<br/>deposit ρ and J"]
    T --> C{"Converged?<br/>or max iterations"}
    C -- no --> E
    C -- yes --> P["Post-process:<br/>fields, trajectories,<br/>screen emittance"]

The electrostatic field is \(\mathbf{E} = -\nabla\phi\) with Dirichlet conditions on metal surfaces (fixed voltage) and Neumann on symmetry planes. The optional magnetostatic field is \(\mathbf{B} = \nabla\times\mathbf{A}\) driven by the beam current. Particles obey \(d\mathbf{p}/dt = q(\mathbf{E} + \mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B})\). The cathode emits according to the Child-Langmuir space-charge-limited law, with the current determined by the local field a short distance in front of the surface, so emission and field settle together.

Convergence is measured as the relative change in the field degrees of freedom between iterations, and the run stops when it drops below the tolerance or when MaxIterations is reached. Current and perveance per iteration are printed so you can see the approach to steady state.

Electron trajectories in a sheet beam klystron gun, colored by momentum, with the focusing electrode and anode.

Benchmark. Gun3P was compared with the commercial code MICHELLE on this gun: both give 129.3 A of emitted current with cathode current densities of 1.75 to 2.4 A/cm², from different mesh types.

docs.title: Input file
docs.text:
Every block and key is described in the Gun3P command syntax.

A .gun3p file has up to four top-level blocks. It shares the ElectrostaticProblem and MagnetostaticProblem block types with TEM3P, and the Tracker block with Track3P; the syntax conventions of each carry over.

dcgun.gun3p (abridged)
DCGunProblem: {
  RunId: test
  SymmetryFactor: 1                   // 1 full, 2 half, 4 quarter
  ElectricRelativeTolerance:  1.00e-12
  ElectricRelativeTolerance2: 1.00e-12  // with magnetic solver active
  MagneticRelativeTolerance:  1.00e-12
  MaxIterations: 32
  Save iteration data: On
}

ElectrostaticProblem: {
  AnodeBoundaryId: 12
  MeshFile: dcgun.ncdf
  BasisOrder: 2
  CurvedSurfaces: on
  Charge averaging factor: 0.1        // under-relaxation of the deposited charge

  VolumeMaterial: {
    Id: 1
    MediumName: Vacuum
    PhysicalParameter: { Name: Permittivity  ConstantValue: 1. }
  }

  Write dofs to disk: on
  Use reduced solver: On
  Outputs: { Dofs for vizualization: On }

  Boundary: { Id: 1   ConditionType: Dirichlet  DirichletValue: 0. }       // cathode
  Boundary: { Id: 2   ConditionType: Dirichlet  DirichletValue: -500. }    // focus electrode
  Boundary: { Id: 12  ConditionType: Dirichlet  DirichletValue: 115000. }  // anode
  Boundary: { Id: 3   ConditionType: Neumann    NeumannValue: 0. }         // open boundary
  Boundary: { Id: 10  ConditionType: Neumann    NeumannValue: 0. }
  Boundary: { Id: 4   ConditionType: Dirichlet  DirichletValue: 0. }

  Compute non zero initial guess: On
  LinearSolver: {
    Solver: CG                        // or MUMPSFLOAT for small problems
    Preconditioner: CHOLESKY
    Tolerance: 1.00e-16
    MaxIterations: 5000
  }
}

MagnetostaticProblem: {
  ...same mesh, materials, and solver pattern; all boundaries Dirichlet 0...
}

Tracker: {
  JobName: ./gun3p_results/OUTPUT
  Particlefile: partpath
  t: 6.0e-6                           // forward tracking time, s
  Generate output for vizualization: on
  Print emission statistics: On
  Backward: { t: 6.0e-6  Generate output for vizualization: on }

  Domain: {
    t0: 0.0
    dt: 1.0e-12
    MaxImpacts: 2
    Emission Nx: 200   Emission Ny: 100   Emission Nz: 300
    Tracking Nx: 200   Tracking Ny: 100   Tracking Nz: 300
    Tracking box x min: -0.11   Tracking box x max: 0.11
    Tracking box y min: -0.04   Tracking box y max: 0.04
    Tracking box z min: -0.001  Tracking box z max: 0.18
  }

  Monitor: {
    Type: PlaneCrossingsVsT
    Name: screen
    Plane point: 0., 0., 0.15999
    Plane normal: 0., 0., 1.
    Compute densities: On
    Max x for densities: 0.110   X number of densities: 11
    Max y for densities: 0.004   Y number of densities: 80
  }

  MeshInterface: { Type: pd  Localizer: { Type: USS_Curve } }

  Emitter: {
    Type: 6                           // Child-Langmuir
    BoundaryID: 1                     // cathode sideset
    N: 1.0e+0                         // electrons per macroparticle
    M: 9.10938e-31                    // kg
    Q: -1.60218e-19                   // C
    d: 0.1e-3                         // macroparticle radius, m
    Sample Type: 1                    // 1 face centers, 2 stochastic
    Child Langmuir: {
      Whole boundary is emitter: On
      Use electric field direction for initial forward velocity: On
      Max allowed total current: 1.35e+9
      Reference z for emission surface: 1.50e-3
      Particles per face: 5
      ...tuning parameters, keep the defaults...
    }
  }

  Material: { BoundarySurfaceID: 1   Type: 2 }   // 2 = Absorber
  Material: { BoundarySurfaceID: 2   Type: 2 }
  Material: { BoundarySurfaceID: 12  Type: 2 }
  ...
}

docs.title: DCGunProblem
docs.text: Key Meaning RunId Label for the run SymmetryFactor 1, 2, or 4. Emitted current is scaled to the full gun. ElectricRelativeTolerance Convergence criterion on the electric field change between iterations, when the magnetic solver is off ElectricRelativeTolerance2, MagneticRelativeTolerance The same when the magnetic solver is on MaxIterations Stop here regardless. The example uses 32; convergence to 10⁻⁵ relative change takes about that many. FirstIterationForMagnetostaticProblem Iteration at which to start including the beam's self-magnetic field. Leave commented out to never run it. JustGenerateTreecotree Run on one core to precompute the tree-cotree gauge for the magnetostatic solve. Needed if the magnetostatic problem fails to converge. Save iteration data Keep per-iteration fields and particles under OUTPUT/ITER_<n>/

docs.title: ElectrostaticProblem and MagnetostaticProblem
docs.text:
These follow the TEM3P conventions: MeshFile, BasisOrder, CurvedSurfaces, one Boundary block per sideset, VolumeMaterial by block. Differences:

Key Meaning AnodeBoundaryId Sideset of the anode. Used to reference the accelerating voltage for perveance. Charge averaging factor Under-relaxation: new charge = (1 − f) × previous + f × computed. 0.1 is stable; larger converges faster if it converges. VolumeMaterial.PhysicalParameter Name is Permittivity, Permeability, or Sigma, with ConstantValue Compute non zero initial guess Start each iteration's solve from the previous solution Use reduced solver Eliminate constrained DOFs before solving. Keep on. Outputs.Dofs for vizualization Write the field for gun3pOutputConverter to turn into a .mod file Outputs.ElectrostaticFieldToken, FileName, Nx, Ny, Nz Also export the field on a Cartesian grid, for use as an external field in Track3P LinearSolver.Solver CG with CHOLESKY for large problems, MUMPSFLOAT for small. Other keys as shown.

In the magnetostatic problem every boundary is Dirichlet 0 and the material parameter is still named Permittivity in the examples, which the code accepts.

docs.title: Tracker
docs.text: Key Meaning JobName Output directory; must match the second argument on the command line t Forward tracking time in s. Make it long enough for the slowest particles to reach the screen. Backward Backward tracking from the emission reference plane to the cathode, used by the Child-Langmuir model to set the launch conditions Domain.dt Tracking time step Domain.Emission Nx/Ny/Nz, Tracking Nx/Ny/Nz Grid resolution for the particle localizer in the emission region and the tracking region Domain.Tracking box ... Bounding box of the tracking region, m. Particles outside are dropped. MeshInterface Localizer settings. Keep as in the example.

docs.title: Emitter
docs.text:
Type: 6 is Child-Langmuir, the model for thermionic DC guns. The other numbered types are shared with Track3P and are listed on its module page.

Key Meaning BoundaryID Cathode sideset N, M, Q Electrons per macroparticle, and the real particle mass and charge d Macroparticle radius for space-charge deposition Sample Type 1 launches from face centers, 2 stochastically across each face Child Langmuir.Reference z for emission surface Distance in front of the cathode at which the field is sampled to set the emission current Child Langmuir.Particles per face Macroparticles launched per cathode face per iteration. Increase for smoother current; the reference says to experiment for convergence. Child Langmuir.Max allowed total current Safety cap in μA

The remaining Child-Langmuir keys control the iteration strategy and are documented as "keep as default" in the command reference.

docs.title: Monitor
docs.text: Type Keys Output PlaneCrossingsVsT Plane point, Plane normal, Compute densities, density grid extents and counts Emittances and current density of particles crossing one plane, printed per iteration PlanesCrossing First plane point, Common plane normal, Distance between first and last planes, Number of planes The same at a stack of parallel planes

docs.title: Material
docs.text: Particle boundary behavior by sideset, numbered: 1 Reflector, 2 Absorber, 3 Secondary emitter, 4 Test surface, 5 SymmetryPlane. In a gun, every metal surface is an absorber.

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
srun -n 256 gun3p dcgun.gun3p gun3p_results

The second argument names the results directory and must agree with Tracker.JobName. The sheet beam gun with 459,000 elements and 32 iterations took 232 s on 256 ranks across two nodes. Each iteration is a full electrostatic solve plus tracking, so the cost scales with iteration count.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Location Content gun3p_results/gun3p.log Timing summary. The detailed iteration log goes to standard output, so keep the Slurm output file. Standard output Per iteration: ||E dofs - prev|| ... rel. tol., emitted current and perveance from the Child-Langmuir model, and the screen monitor's emittances OUTPUT/previousPerveanceAtIter<n> Micro-perveance after each iteration, one number per file OUTPUT/emissionMap<n> Emission current per cathode face OUTPUT/ITER_<n>/E/, PARTICLES/ Per-iteration fields and trajectories when Save iteration data is on OUTPUT/E/, OUTPUT/M/ Final electrostatic and magnetostatic DOFs; staticDofs.ncdf.mod appears after the converter runs OUTPUT/PARTICLES/partpath_ts<n>.ncdf Particle positions per time step of the final iteration, for animation

docs.title: Post-processing
docs.text:
The fields are stored as DOF vectors. Convert them to ParaView .mod files with the companion program:

gun3pOutputConverter dcgun.gun3p e        # electric field, final iteration
gun3pOutputConverter dcgun.gun3p m        # magnetic field
gun3pOutputConverter dcgun.gun3p e 30     # electric field at iteration 30

Output goes to OUTPUT/E/staticDofs.ncdf.mod and OUTPUT/M/. If ElectrostaticFieldToken was on, the converter also writes the field on the Cartesian grid as a text file, which Track3P reads through Domain.ElectroStaticFieldMap. The Track3P module page describes that coupling.

In ParaView, load the mesh with the .mod file for the field and the partpath_ts*.ncdf series for the trajectories.

docs.title: Tutorial
docs.text: Sheet beam klystron gun: a 115 kV DC gun with a focus electrode, run to self-consistency and compared with MICHELLE.

docs.title: Gun3P tutorial: sheet beam klystron gun
docs.text:
Example directory: examples/gun3p/LSBK

A DC gun for a sheet beam klystron: a wide, flat cathode at ground, a focus electrode at −500 V, and an anode at 115 kV. The beam exits through the anode aperture toward a screen 16 cm downstream. Gun3P finds the self-consistent emitted current and the beam shape at the screen.

The full-model mesh, and the electrostatic potential: anode (red, 115 kV), cathode and focus electrode (blue, near 0 V).

docs.title: Mesh from a STEP file
docs.text:
Unlike the other tutorials, this geometry arrives as a CAD STEP file rather than a Cubit journal. The journal imports and heals it, refines the cathode surfaces, meshes, and assigns sidesets by explicit surface lists.

dcgun.jou
reset
import step "SBK_3D.step" heal

surface 1 size 3                           # cathode
surface 47 size 3
volume all scheme tetmesh
vol 1 sizing function skeleton scale 3 min_size 0.1 max_size 7 max_gradient 1.3
mesh volume all

sideset 1 surface 1 47                     # cathode
sideset 2 surface 33 12 3 23 32 31 48 49 22 21 10 11   # focus electrode
sideset 3 surface 34                       # open boundary
sideset 4 surface 2 36
sideset 12 surface 4 5 6 7 8 9 13 14 15 16 17 18 19 20 24 25 26 27 28 29 30 35 37 38 40 41 42 43 44 45 46   # anode
sideset 10 surface 39                      # open boundary

block 1 volume 1
block all element type tetra10
volume all scale 0.001
export genesis "dcgun.gen" overwrite

import step ... heal repairs small CAD defects on import. The result is 459,206 elements with boundary IDs 1, 2, 3, 4, 10, 12. Long explicit surface lists like the anode's are fragile; for your own models prefer Cubit groups selected by coordinate or by name, as the Cubit page describes.

The cathode, focus electrode, and anode nose. The mesh is refined at the cathode where emission is computed.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
The full file is shown on the module page. The decisions it encodes:

  • Full model, SymmetryFactor: 1. The gun is not symmetric enough in its CAD representation to cut.
  • Voltages. Cathode 0 V, focus electrode −500 V, anode 115 kV. The small negative bias on the focus electrode shapes the beam edge.
  • Both field solvers. MagnetostaticProblem is present, so the beam's self-magnetic field is included once FirstIterationForMagnetostaticProblem is reached. In the shipped file that key is commented out, so the magnetostatic solve is set up but never activated; the run is electrostatic only.
  • 32 iterations, with the fields and particles of each saved.
  • Screen at z = 0.15999 m, just before the exit boundary at 0.16, collecting emittances and current density on an 11 by 80 grid.
  • Child-Langmuir emission from the whole cathode, five macroparticles per face, each representing one electron, with a 0.1 mm space-charge radius.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
srun -n 256 gun3p dcgun.gun3p gun3p_results

The run completed in 232 s on 256 ranks. Standard output carries the iteration history; gun3p_results/gun3p.log has only the timing summary.

docs.title: Convergence
docs.text:
The emitted current and micro-perveance from the Child-Langmuir model, per iteration:

Iteration Emitted current (A) Micro-perveance (μA/V3/2) 0 562.6 7.21 1 475.1 7.21 2 370.1 9.70 8 124.1 8.39 16 127.5 4.04 24 128.4 3.18 31 128.4 3.29

The first guess, with no space charge in the field, over-emits by a factor of four. Space charge builds up over the first ten iterations and suppresses the emission to its self-consistent value of 128.4 A, after which the current is steady and only the field keeps refining. The relative change in the electric field falls from 2.4×10⁻³ at iteration 1 to 1.6×10⁻⁵ at iteration 31, far from the 10⁻¹² tolerance in the input, so the run ended on MaxIterations. That is normal: the tolerance in the shipped file is unreachable in double precision, and 10⁻⁵ is well converged for engineering purposes.

Total emitted current and relative field error against iteration, from the workshop slides. The current settles by iteration 12; the field continues to converge geometrically.

docs.title: Comparison with MICHELLE
docs.text:
The same gun was simulated with MICHELLE, a commercial finite-element gun code. From the published comparison:

Quantity Gun3P MICHELLE Elements 1,316,530 tetrahedra 1,073,000 hexahedra Basis order 2 1 Emitted current 129.3 A 129.3 A Cathode current density 1.75 to 2.36 A/cm² 1.75 to 2.40 A/cm² Beam hitting electrodes 0 % 0 % Run time 5.5 h on 48 cores 63.6 h on 1 core

The tutorial's coarser 459,000-element mesh gives 128.4 A, within 0.7 percent of the fine-mesh value.

docs.title: Post-process
docs.text:
gun3pOutputConverter dcgun.gun3p e
gun3pOutputConverter dcgun.gun3p m

writes OUTPUT/E/staticDofs.ncdf.mod and the magnetic equivalent. In ParaView, load dcgun.ncdf with that .mod file for the potential and field, and add the OUTPUT/PARTICLES/partpath_ts*.ncdf series to animate the beam from cathode to screen. The screen monitor's emittances are in the standard output, labelled plane monitor 'screen', in π mm·mrad.

docs.title: Variations
docs.text:
• Turn on the self-magnetic field. Uncomment FirstIterationForMagnetostaticProblem: 1 or set it to an iteration after the current has settled. For a 129 A beam the magnetic self-pinch is not negligible.
  • Trim the iterations. The current is converged by iteration 12. Set MaxIterations accordingly and halve the run time, or raise Charge averaging factor cautiously to converge in fewer.
  • Export the field for Track3P. Add ElectrostaticFieldToken: On with a FileName and Nx, Ny, Nz to Outputs, rerun the converter, and the Cartesian field file can be loaded in Track3P as a static field alongside an RF field. The Coax-StaticField example under examples/track3p does exactly this.
  • Electrostatic only. Remove the Tracker block and set MaxIterations: 0 to use Gun3P as a plain electrostatic solver for electrode design.

docs.title: Omega3P
docs.text:
Omega3P computes the resonant modes of an RF cavity: the eigenfrequencies, the quality factors, and the electromagnetic field distribution of each mode. It is the most widely used ACE3P module and the starting point for most other analyses, since Track3P, TEM3P, and the acdtool RF post-processor all consume its output.

Cavities analyzed in the tutorials: rounded pillbox, coax coupler, waveguide coupler with lossy load, and a traveling-wave cell.

docs.title: What it solves
docs.text:
In the frequency domain, Maxwell's equations in a source-free cavity reduce to the vector wave equation for the electric field:

\[ \nabla \times \left(\mu^{-1} \nabla \times \mathbf{E}\right) - \omega^2 \varepsilon\, \mathbf{E} = 0 \]

Discretizing with high-order Nédélec vector finite elements gives a generalized eigenvalue problem \(K\mathbf{x} = \lambda M\mathbf{x}\) with \(\lambda = \omega^2\). Omega3P handles three cases:

Case Eigenvalue When Lossless, closed cavity Real Perfect electric or magnetic walls, periodic boundaries. Wall loss and Q0 are computed afterward by perturbation from the surface conductivity. Open or lossy cavity Complex Waveguide ports, absorbing boundaries, lossy dielectrics, surface impedance. The imaginary part gives the external or dielectric Q. Multiple ports with different cutoffs Nonlinear Each port adds a frequency-dependent term. Solved with the CORK rational Krylov method.

The frequency is \(f = \omega / 2\pi\) and, for a complex eigenvalue, \(Q = \mathrm{Re}(f) / 2\,\mathrm{Im}(f)\).

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
• Perfect electric and magnetic boundary conditions for symmetry reduction
  • Periodic boundaries with an arbitrary phase advance, for dispersion curves of traveling-wave structures
  • Waveguide ports with modal expansion, for coupler external Q
  • Absorbing boundaries for simple beam-pipe truncation
  • Volume materials with complex permittivity, for loads and windows
  • Surface conductivity for wall-loss Q0, and surface impedance for coatings
  • Finite-element orders 1 through 6 on curved tetrahedra
  • Adaptive mesh refinement driven by an error estimate
  • Checkpoint and restart of long eigensolves

docs.title: Input file
docs.text:
The input <project>.omega3p uses the common blocks plus EigenSolver and, for open cavities, one Port block per port. A complete lossless example:

pillbox.omega3p
ModelInfo : {
  File: ./pillbox4.ncdf
  BoundaryCondition : {
    Magnetic: 1, 2
    Exterior: 6
  }
  SurfaceMaterial : {
    ReferenceNumber: 6
    Sigma: 5.8e7
  }
}

FiniteElement: {
  Order:           2
  CurvedSurfaces: on
}

EigenSolver : {
  NumEigenvalues: 2
  FrequencyShift:  1.0e9
}

PostProcess : {
  Toggle: on
  ModeFile: mode
}

docs.title: EigenSolver block
docs.text:
Key Default Meaning NumEigenvalues 1 How many modes to find, counting upward in frequency from FrequencyShift FrequencyShift 10 GHz Target frequency. The solver finds the modes nearest to and above this value. Set it a little below the lowest mode you want. FrequencyShiftImag 0 Imaginary part of the shift, for complex problems Tolerance 1e-8 Relative residual for eigenpair convergence MaxIterations 200 Krylov iteration limit SolverMode automatic Choose the algorithm explicitly: Arnoldi, InexactLanczos, ESIL, SOAR, CORK. Automatic picks by problem type. CORK Sub-block with TargetFrequencyMin, TargetFrequencyMax, TargetFrequencyImag, ApproxTolerance, ApproxMaxDegree for the nonlinear solver. See Tutorial 2.

The full list, including adaptive refinement and matrix dump options, is in the Omega3P keyword reference, and every block is described key by key in the Omega3P command syntax.

When is a multi-port problem quadratic, and when nonlinear?

With waveguide ports the eigenproblem is quadratic, and the default solver handles it, when every port loads one mode and all ports share the same cutoff frequency. The CW23 slides give the example of a pillbox whose waveguide coupler and both beam-pipe ends are all declared Waveguide with one mode each. When ports have different cutoffs, or several modes per port, the problem is nonlinear and there are three options in increasing accuracy and cost: the 1D Absorbing boundary (an approximation), a PML (a good approximation, see the command syntax), or the CORK nonlinear solver (accurate but harder to converge).

docs.title: Port block
docs.text:
Port : {
  ReferenceNumber : 7     // sideset of the port surface
  NumberOfModes : 1       // waveguide modes to load at this port
}

A surface listed under Waveguide in BoundaryCondition must have a matching Port block, or Omega3P loads one mode by default. The port is treated as matched for every loaded mode. Choosing how many modes to load is discussed in Tutorial 2.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Results go into omega3p_results/ next to the input file.

File Content omega3p.out Full log: parsed input, mesh statistics, DOF count, iteration history, and a Mode block per eigenpair with Frequency, QualityFactor, ExternalQ, TotalEnergy, PowerLoss, and the field file name omega3p.log Shorter progress log omega3p.warn Warnings. Read this if a result is unexpected. omega3p.l0.m0000.<freq>.mod Field file for mode 0 at refinement level 0. One per mode. For complex problems the name carries R<real>.I<imag>. 2dports.log Cutoff frequencies and types of the waveguide modes computed on each port surface VECTOR/ Raw eigenvectors

A typical mode summary:

Mode : {
    TotalEnergy : 4.2137588190101e-12 , 0
    ExternalQ : 267.27097453785
    QualityFactor : 26238.857067312
    File : omega3p_results/omega3p.l0.m0000.R1.1762928e+09.I2.2005621e+06.mod
    PowerLoss : 1.1869161916105e-06
    Frequency : 1176292763.7678 , 2200562.1182804
}

QualityFactor is the wall-loss Q0 from SurfaceMaterial. ExternalQ is from the ports and is only present for complex problems. The two Frequency numbers are the real and imaginary parts in hertz.

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text:
1. Pillbox cavity: the complete workflow from Cubit journal to R/Q, plus a mesh convergence study.
  2. Coax and waveguide couplers: waveguide ports, external Q, and the nonlinear eigenproblem with two ports.
  3. Lossy load and periodic boundaries: multiple materials with complex permittivity, and a dispersion point of a disk-loaded structure.

Post-processing with acdtool postprocess rf has its own page: Post-processing.

docs.title: Post-processing with acdtool
docs.text:
ParaView shows field patterns. For numbers such as shunt impedance, kick factor, and peak surface fields, use the RF post-processor built into acdtool:

acdtool postprocess rf <project>.rfpost

It runs serially and reads the mode files that Omega3P or S3P wrote. Running it with no file argument writes a sample.rfpost template containing every available function with default values, which is the easiest way to start.

docs.title: The .rfpost file
docs.text:
The file is a sequence of named blocks. The first must be RFField, which selects the mode and sets scaling. Every other block is a calculation that is enabled with ionoff = 1.

pillbox-rtop.rfpost
RFField
{
   ResultDir   = omega3p_results   // where the .mod files are
   FreqScanID  = 0                 // S3P only: frequency scan index
   ModeID      = 0                 // which mode, when a block uses modeID = -1
   xsymmetry   = magnetic          // [none, electric, magnetic]
   ysymmetry   = magnetic
   gradient    = 2.0e7             // V/m; -1 keeps normalized fields
   cavityBeta  = 1.0               // particle beta for V and R/Q integrals
   reversePowerFlow = 0            // [1 = charging, 0 = decaying]
   x0 = 0.0                        // integration axis x
   y0 = 0.0                        // integration axis y
   gz1 = -0.057                    // integration start z, m
   gz2 =  0.057                    // integration end z, m
   npoint = 300                    // points along the axis
   fmnx = 10                       // field map resolution
   fmny = 10
   fmnz = 50
}

RoverQ
{
   ionoff = 1
   modeID1 = -1                    // -1, -1: all modes
   modeID2 = -1
   x1 = 0.0
   x2 = 0.0
   y1 = 0.001
   y2 = 0.001
   z1 = 1e8                        // 1e8: use the model bounding box
   z2 = 1e8
}

maxFieldsOnSurface
{
   ionoff = 1
   surfaceID = 6
}

docs.title: RFField keys
docs.text: Key Meaning ResultDir Results directory from the solver ModeID Mode used by single-mode functions xsymmetry, ysymmetry Tell the post-processor which symmetry planes were used so volume integrals are scaled to the full cavity gradient Accelerating gradient in V/m used to scale fields. With -1, fields keep the solver's normalization of 1 J stored energy. cavityBeta Particle velocity for the transit-time factor in V and R/Q gz1, gz2 Axial integration range for the voltage. Set to the cavity length, not the whole beam pipe, to define the gradient consistently.

docs.title: Functions
docs.text:
Block Computes RoverQ Voltage along a line and R/Q = V²/(ωU) per mode RoverQT Transverse R/Q kickFactor Transverse kick factor FieldMap Field on a 3D grid of nx × ny × nz points in the given box FieldAtPoint, ALLFieldAtPoint Field at one point, for one or all modes FieldOnLine, ALLFieldOnLine Field along a line with npoint samples at a given rfphase, written to filename fieldOn2DBoundary Field on a boundary surface, written to file fieldOnSurface Field on a surface as components or amplitude maxFieldsOnSurface Peak E and H on a surface with their locations Multipole analysis Multipole decomposition of the field on axis

Coordinates are in meters. A coordinate of 1e8 means "use the bounding box of the model," which is convenient for line integrals along the full axis.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
acdtool writes to standard output and to rfpost.out. It begins with a mode summary:

** Omega3P/S3P Mode Summary:
**   Total number of modes :      2
**      ModeID         Frequency(r,i)                       Qext
**         0           1.31381e+09, 0.00000e+00           0.00000e+00
**         1           2.32914e+09, 0.00000e+00           0.00000e+00
**   Model bounding box: ( 0.00000e+00,  0.00000e+00 -1.50000e-01)
**                       ( 1.00005e-01,  1.00123e-01  1.50000e-01)

followed by a [scaling] block giving the voltage and the factor used to scale the normalized fields to the requested gradient, then one block per enabled function:

[RoverQ]
{  // RoverQ=V^2/(omega*U)
 ModeID  Frequency           (V_r, V_i)                      |V|            RoQ(ohm/cavity)
    0   1.31381e+09  ( 2.2980e+00,  3.4925e+00)    4.18073e+00      1.19567e+02
    1   2.32914e+09  (-7.2671e-04,  6.2729e-04)    9.59998e-04      3.55621e-06
}

[maxFieldsOnSurface]
{
   surfaceID :   6
      ModeID :   0
        Emax :  4.22488e+07 (V/m)   at ( 3.9627e-02,  1.8486e-02, -4.5454e-02)
        Hmax :  5.80786e+04 (A/m)   at ( 3.3116e-02,  7.9193e-02,  3.2771e-02)
}

Surface field values correspond to the gradient in RFField. The ratio Epeak/Eacc is a standard figure of merit and comes straight from Emax divided by gradient.

R/Q convention

acdtool reports R/Q in the circuit convention V²/(ωU) in ohms per cavity, where V is the full on-axis voltage after the transit-time factor. For a symmetric model the xsymmetry and ysymmetry settings restore the full-cavity stored energy. Divide by 2 for the linac convention if your comparison uses it.

docs.title: S3P results
docs.text: The same tool works on S3P output. Set FreqScanID to pick a frequency point from the scan and ModeID to pick the excited port mode.

docs.title: Tutorial 3: lossy load and periodic boundaries
docs.text: Two further Omega3P features: a second material with complex permittivity, which absorbs power and produces a complex eigenvalue without any port, and periodic boundary conditions for one cell of a traveling-wave structure.

docs.title: Part A: waveguide coupler with a lossy load
docs.text:
Example directory: examples/omega3p/pillbox+recWG+load

Instead of terminating the waveguide of Tutorial 2 with a port, fill its end with a lossy dielectric. The journal step3-ADD-load.jou webcuts the guide at y = 200 mm so the far section becomes a separate volume.

docs.title: Imprint and merge
docs.text:
Two volumes that touch must share a single interface surface, otherwise the mesh is disconnected across it and the solver sees two separate cavities. Cubit does this with imprint and merge:

reset
import acis "pillbox+recWG+load.sat"
imprint body 1 2
merge body 1 2
volume all scheme Tetmesh
volume 1 sizing function type skeleton scale 7 time_accuracy_level 2 min_size auto max_size 15 max_gradient 1.2
volume 2 sizing function type skeleton scale 7 time_accuracy_level 2 min_size auto max_size 10 max_gradient 1.2
mesh volume all

Sideset 1 surface 4 20
Sideset 2 surface 9
Sideset 6 surface all except 4 20 9 1

block 1 volume 1          # vacuum
block 2 volume 2          # load
block all element type tetra10
volume all scale 0.001
export Genesis "pillbox+recWG+load.gen" block all overwrite

Each volume goes in its own block so the solver can assign different materials. The load gets a finer mesh since the wavelength inside a high-permittivity material is shorter.

After imprint and merge, the interface between guide and load is one surface. Verify this in Cubit before export.

docs.title: Input with two materials
Results
docs.text:
Eigenvalue: (591.2395988707802, 0.1200579050951992)
        Frequency: (1160172571.152617, 117793.09714004)
Eigenvalue: (600.8495902547749, 90.41431550096833)
        Frequency: (1172850486.101091, 87749817.12126675)

Mode 0 at 1.160 GHz has a small imaginary part, Q of about 4900 from the load, and is the cavity mode. Mode 1 at 1.173 GHz has an imaginary part of 88 MHz, Q below 10, and lives mostly in the load. Heavily damped modes like this appear whenever a lossy volume is present; recognize them by their very low Q and by inspecting the field in ParaView.

docs.title: Part B: periodic boundaries for a disk-loaded structure
docs.text:
Example directory: examples/omega3p/dlwg-pbc

One cell of a disk-loaded waveguide as a quarter model and as an eighth model.

A traveling-wave accelerator structure is periodic. Rather than model many cells, simulate one with a periodic boundary condition: the field on the exit face equals the field on the entry face times a phase factor \(e^{-j\theta}\). Sweeping the phase advance \(\theta\) gives the dispersion curve.

docs.title: Mesh the master and slave faces identically
docs.text:
The periodic condition maps each node on the master face to a node on the slave face, so the two surface meshes must be the same. Mesh the master surface first, copy its mesh to the slave with matching curve and vertex pairs, then mesh the volume.

step2a-pbc-mesh_1fourth.jou
reset
import acis "ds-cell-1fourth.sat"
volume 1 scheme tetmesh
volume 1 size 2.0
surface 5 6 size 1.          # nose cone
surface 9 size 1.            # iris

mesh surface 2               # master face
copy Mesh Surface 2 Onto Surface 4 source curve 10 target curve 17 source vertex 9 target vertex 10 Nosmoothing
mesh volume 1

sideset 3 surface 2          # Periodic_M
sideset 4 surface 4          # Periodic_S
sideset 1 surface 3
sideset 2 surface 1
sideset 6 surface all except 2 4 3 1

block 1 vol all
block 1 element type tetra10
transform mesh output scale 0.001
export genesis "pbc-4.gen" overwrite

Warning

Do not smooth the mesh after copying, and do not let a volume smoother move the periodic faces. The Nosmoothing option and the commented-out smooth lines in the example are deliberate.

docs.title: Input with a phase advance
Dispersion curve
docs.text:
Run the same mesh with Theta at several values between 0 and 180 and plot frequency against phase advance. The 0 and 180 degree points are the band edges and can also be obtained with the ordinary magnetic and electric boundary conditions on the two faces; use that as a cross-check of the periodic implementation.

The example includes dlwg-pbc4-m1.omega3p, which switches one symmetry plane to Electric to pick the dipole band instead of the monopole band, and dlwg-pbc8-m0.omega3p for the eighth model.

docs.title: Tutorial 1: pillbox cavity
docs.text:
This tutorial runs the complete ACE3P workflow on the simplest useful cavity: a pillbox with rounded top and beam pipes. You will build and mesh the geometry in Cubit, convert the mesh, compute the two lowest monopole modes with Omega3P, look at the fields in ParaView, extract R/Q and peak surface fields with acdtool, and finish with a mesh convergence study.

Example directory: examples/omega3p/pillbox-rtop

Parameter Value Cavity length 90 mm Cavity radius 100 mm Beam pipe radius 35 mm Beam pipe length 300 mm total Iris rounding 12 mm Top rounding 45 mm

Expected result: the TM010 mode at 1.3138 GHz with Q0 of 28,885 for copper walls.

docs.title: Step 1: Build the geometry
docs.text:
The journal step1-Make-pillbox-rtop.jou builds the full cavity, then cuts it to a quarter model using the two symmetry planes.

step1-Make-pillbox-rtop.jou
reset
#{cav_length = 90}
#{cav_radius = 100}
#{bp_length  = 300}
#{bp_radius  = 35 }
#{iris_rounding = 12}

create Cylinder height {cav_length} radius {cav_radius}
create Cylinder height {bp_length} radius {bp_radius}
unite volume all
compress ids
modify curve 6 5  blend radius {iris_rounding}
modify curve 1 2 blend radius {0.5*cav_length}
export acis "pillbox-rtop0.sat" overwrite

webcut volume 1 with plane xplane offset 0 noimprint nomerge
delete volume 2
compress ids
webcut volume 1 with plane yplane offset 0 noimprint nomerge
delete volume 1
compress ids
export acis "pillbox-rtop4.sat" overwrite

Lines starting with #{...} define Cubit variables, so dimensions can be changed in one place. The full model is saved as pillbox-rtop0.sat before cutting, so it can be reused when adding couplers in Tutorial 2. The quarter model is pillbox-rtop4.sat.

Run it in Cubit with the Play button, or through Tools, then Journal Editor.

docs.title: Step 2: Mesh
docs.text:
step2-Mesh-pillbox-rtop.jou
reset
import acis "pillbox-rtop4.sat"

volume all scheme Tetmesh
volume all sizing function type skeleton scale 5 time_accuracy_level 2 min_size auto max_size 12 max_gradient 1.2
mesh volume all

Sideset 1 surface 7
Sideset 2 surface 1
Sideset 6 surface all except 7 1

block 1 volume all
block 1 element type tetra10

volume all scale 0.001
export Genesis "pillbox-rtop4.gen" block all overwrite

Sidesets 1 and 2 are the two symmetry planes. Sideset 6 is every other surface, which is the cavity wall. The element type must be tetra10 and the model is scaled from millimeters to meters just before export.

The meshed quarter model. The Cubit command window reports 13,258 elements and three sidesets.

docs.title: Step 3: Convert the mesh
docs.text:
Copy pillbox-rtop4.gen to your working directory on the HPC system and convert it:

acdtool meshconvert pillbox-rtop4.gen

Check the statistics it prints. You want Euler Char is OK, boundary IDs 1 2 6, one material ID, and zero invalid second-order elements. The meaning of each line is explained in Mesh preparation.

docs.title: Step 4: Write the Omega3P input
Step 5: Run Omega3P
docs.text:
Submit a batch job with the header for your system from Getting started. The solver line is:

srun -n 16 omega3p pillbox-rtop.omega3p

For this mesh, 16 ranks finish in about one minute. Watch progress with squeue -u $USER and tail -f on the Slurm output file.

docs.title: Step 6: Read the results
docs.text:
Look in omega3p_results/:

omega3p.l0.m0000.1.3138129e+09.mod
omega3p.l0.m0001.2.3291363e+09.mod
omega3p.log
omega3p.out
omega3p.warn
VECTOR/

The mode frequencies are already in the file names. In omega3p.out, the mode summary gives the details:

Mode : {
    TotalEnergy : 4.4270939088102e-12
    QualityFactor : 28885.092644708
    File : omega3p_results/omega3p.l0.m0000.1.3138100e+09.mod
    PowerLoss : 1.2651947886823e-06
    Frequency : 1313809979.5477
}
Mode : {
    TotalEnergy : 4.4270939088102e-12
    QualityFactor : 33830.795068362
    File : omega3p_results/omega3p.l0.m0001.2.3291386e+09.mod
    PowerLoss : 1.9150571359106e-06
    Frequency : 2329138623.836
}

Mode 0 at 1.3138 GHz is TM010 with Q0 of 28,885 for copper walls. Mode 1 at 2.329 GHz is the next monopole mode. Above the summary, the log records the DOF count, which you will need for the convergence study:

*   Total Number of Elements used:  13382
*   Total Number of DOFs:   82592

docs.title: Step 7: Visualize in ParaView
docs.text:
Copy the mesh and the mode files back to your laptop:

scp <user>@<host>:<dir>/pillbox-rtop4.ncdf .
scp '<user>@<host>:<dir>/omega3p_results/*.mod' .

In ParaView with the SLAC toolbar enabled, click the SLAC folder icon, select the mesh file and a mode file, and Apply.

Color the external surface by efield magnitude to see the field pattern. For TM010 the field peaks on axis in the cavity and at the iris.

For an arrow plot, apply Filters, Alphabetical, Glyph with efield as the vector. To look through the symmetry plane, select External Surface, apply Extract Block, and keep only the dataset for the wall.

The Line plot button on the SLAC toolbar plots a field component along a line, typically the beam axis.

docs.title: Step 8: Post-process with acdtool
docs.text:
Shunt impedance, kick factor, and peak surface fields come from acdtool postprocess rf, driven by an .rfpost file. The example directory contains pillbox-rtop.rfpost with RoverQ and maxFieldsOnSurface enabled. Run:

srun -n 1 acdtool postprocess rf pillbox-rtop.rfpost

Output for the two modes:

[RoverQ]
 ModeID  Frequency           (V_r, V_i)                     |V|           RoQ(ohm/cavity)
    0   1.31381e+09  ( 2.2980e+00,  3.4925e+00)    4.18073e+00      1.19567e+02
    1   2.32914e+09  (-7.2671e-04,  6.2729e-04)    9.59998e-04      3.55621e-06

[maxFieldsOnSurface]
   surfaceID :   6
      ModeID :   0
        Emax :  4.22488e+07 (V/m)   at ( 3.9627e-02,  1.8486e-02, -4.5454e-02)
        Hmax :  5.80786e+04 (A/m)   at ( 3.3116e-02,  7.9193e-02,  3.2771e-02)

R/Q of about 120 ohm per cavity for TM010, and essentially zero for mode 1, which has no net on-axis voltage. Peak fields are scaled to the gradient given in the RFField block. The .rfpost file format and all available functions are described in Post-processing.

docs.title: Convergence study
docs.text:
A single mesh tells you nothing about accuracy. The directory includes mesh0.jou through mesh3.jou, identical except for the sizing function scale, which is 10, 8, 6, and 4 respectively, so mesh0 is the coarsest and mesh3 the finest. The input file mesh-conv.omega3p reads mesh0.ncdf; edit the file name for each level.

Run all four meshes and record the TM010 frequency and element count from each omega3p.out. Treat the finest mesh as the reference and plot the relative frequency error against element count.

With order 2 elements, the frequency converges to a few parts in 105 by about 20,000 elements. Use this kind of plot to decide how fine a mesh you need for a given accuracy target, and remember that surface fields converge more slowly than frequency.

Order versus mesh density

Raising FiniteElement.Order from 2 to 3 on the same mesh often gains more accuracy per DOF than refining the mesh. The workflow assistant page shows an automated order-convergence sweep on this cavity.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text: examples/omega3p/omega3p-exercise-1 contains a 1.5-cell gun geometry with target dimensions. Build it, find the pi mode, and adjust the cell dimensions so the mode frequency is correct and the field is balanced between cells.

docs.title: Tutorial 2: couplers and waveguide ports
docs.text: Real cavities have couplers. A coupler turns the lossless eigenproblem into a complex one: energy leaves through the port, the eigenfrequency acquires an imaginary part, and the external Q follows. This tutorial adds a coax coupler and then a waveguide coupler to the pillbox from Tutorial 1, and ends with a two-port case that requires the nonlinear eigensolver.

docs.title: Part A: coax coupler
docs.text:
Example directory: examples/omega3p/pillbox-rtop+coax

Coax dimension Value Inner conductor radius 8.7 mm Outer conductor radius 20 mm Axial position z = 100 mm Inner conductor tip 30 mm from beam axis Tip rounding 5 mm Outer-to-beampipe rounding 7 mm

docs.title: Build in steps
docs.text:
Complex models are easiest to build incrementally. Reuse the full pillbox saved in Tutorial 1, add the coax, then cut to a half model. Only one symmetry plane survives because the coupler breaks the other.

step2-ADD-coax.jou
reset
create Cylinder height 120 radius 20
create Cylinder height 120 radius 8.7
body 1 2 rotate 90 about y
body 1 2 move -60 0 100
body 2 move -30 0 0
import acis "pillbox-rtop0.sat"
unite body 1 3
compress ids
subtract body 2 from 1
compress ids
modify curve 10 blend radius 7
modify curve 12 blend radius 5
export acis "pillbox-rtop+coax.sat" overwrite
webcut volume 1 with plane yplane offset 0
delete body 1
compress ids
export acis "pillbox-rtop+coax2.sat" overwrite

docs.title: Mesh with a port sideset
docs.text:
step3-Mesh-pillbox-rtop+coax.jou
reset
import acis "pillbox-rtop+coax2.sat"
volume all scheme Tetmesh
volume all sizing function type skeleton scale 7 time_accuracy_level 2 min_size auto max_size 15 max_gradient 1.5
mesh volume all
Sideset 2 surface 1            # symmetry plane
Sideset 3 surface 3            # beam pipe end
Sideset 4 surface 2            # beam pipe end
Sideset 7 surface 17           # coax port
Sideset 6 surface all except 1 3 2 17
block 1 volume all
block 1 element type tetra10
volume all scale 0.001
export Genesis "pillbox-rtop+coax2.gen" block all overwrite

The coax end surface gets its own sideset, 7, so it can be declared a port. The beam pipe ends are 3 and 4.

docs.title: Input with a port
Run and read
docs.text:
Convert, run, and post-process exactly as in Tutorial 1. The mode summary now has a complex frequency and an external Q. From the example's stored results:

Mode : {
    TotalEnergy : 4.4270939088102e-12 , 0
    ExternalQ : 1024235.9558753
    QualityFactor : 28815.235456204
    File : omega3p_results/omega3p.l0.m0000.R1.3137561e+09.I6.4133469e+02.mod
    PowerLoss : 1.2682100135575e-06
    Frequency : 1313756106.8639 , 641.33469408486
}

ExternalQ is the coupler Qext, here about 1.0 million: with the inner conductor tip 30 mm from the axis, this coax barely couples to TM010. QualityFactor is still the wall Q0, essentially unchanged from the closed cavity. The loaded Q is \(1/Q_L = 1/Q_0 + 1/Q_{ext}\), and the imaginary part of the frequency is \(f_r / 2 Q_L\). Pushing the probe deeper toward the axis lowers Qext rapidly; the hands-on exercise in Part B does the equivalent for a waveguide iris.

docs.title: Port modes in ParaView
docs.text: Omega3P writes the 2D port mode it computed on the port surface to omega3p_results/port7/mode_1.00000GHz_000.vtu. Load the 3D mesh with the SLAC toolbar, then File, Open the .vtu file and color by Ereal. Switch to wireframe if the port surface hides behind the wall.

docs.title: Part B: rectangular waveguide coupler
docs.text:
Example directory: examples/omega3p/pillbox+recWG

A waveguide coupler attaches a rectangular guide to the cavity through an iris. The journal step2-ADD-recWG-to-pillbox.jou parameterizes the guide width wguide, height hguide, iris width wiris, and iris depth diris, builds the guide as two bricks, unites with the full pillbox, rounds the iris corners, and cuts to a quarter model. The waveguide end becomes sideset 7.

The input is the same shape as the coax case:

BoundaryCondition : {
  Magnetic:  1, 2
  Electric:  3, 4
  Exterior:  6
  Waveguide: 7
}
Port : {
  ReferenceNumber : 7
  NumberOfModes : 1          // TE10 of the rectangular guide
}

A rectangular guide, unlike a coax, has a nonzero cutoff. Omega3P computes the guide's modes on the port surface numerically and writes them to 2dports.log. Check that the TE10 cutoff is below the cavity frequency, otherwise the port is not actually propagating.

docs.title: Absorbing boundary alternative
docs.text:
If modal accuracy at the port does not matter, a first-order absorbing boundary is simpler:

BoundaryCondition : {
  ...
  Absorbing: 7
}
Port : {
  ReferenceNumber : 7
  CutoffFrequency : 1e9      // phase velocity from this cutoff
}

Without a Port block, the absorbing boundary assumes a phase velocity of \(c\). With CutoffFrequency, it uses the guide's phase velocity at the eigenfrequency. The absorbing boundary is less accurate than a waveguide port with modal expansion and should be reserved for beam-pipe truncation.

docs.title: Hands-on
docs.text: Change wiris in the journal, remesh, rerun, and find the iris width that gives Qext of about 4000. Two or three iterations usually bracket it.

docs.title: Part C: two ports with different cutoffs
docs.text:
Example directory: examples/omega3p/pillbox+recWG+cirWG

Add a circular waveguide on the beam axis to the Part B model. Now there are two ports, each with several modes near the cavity frequency and with different cutoffs. The waveguide boundary term depends on frequency through \(\sqrt{\omega^2 - \omega_c^2}\) for each loaded mode, and with more than one distinct cutoff the eigenproblem is no longer quadratic. Omega3P solves it with CORK, a rational Krylov method.

in1.omega3p (EigenSolver and Port blocks)
EigenSolver : {
  NumEigenvalues:  3
  Tolerance:       1e-10
  FrequencyShift:  1.0e9
  SolverMode:      CORK
  CORK : {
    TargetFrequencyMin:   1.0e9    // search window, real part
    TargetFrequencyMax:   2.4e9
    TargetFrequencyImag:  5.0e8    // search window, imaginary part
    MaxIterations:        500
    ApproxTolerance:      1e-12    // rational approximation accuracy
    ApproxMaxDegree:      100
  }
}

Port : {
  ReferenceNumber : 4            // circular guide
  NumberOfModes : 10
}
Port : {
  ReferenceNumber : 7            // rectangular guide
  NumberOfModes : 10
}

CORK searches a rectangle in the complex frequency plane rather than expanding around a single shift, so you give it a window instead of a target. Start by loading generously many port modes, here 10 per port, so no propagating mode is missed.

docs.title: Check the port modes
docs.text:
After the run, 2dports.log lists each port's modes with cutoff frequency and type. For this geometry:

Mode Port 4 (circular) Port 7 (rectangular) 1 TM 1.043 GHz TE 0.908 GHz 2 TE 1.325 GHz TE 1.897 GHz 3 TM 2.228 GHz TM 1.897 GHz 4 TE 2.307 GHz TE 2.726 GHz 5 TM 2.395 GHz TE 3.194 GHz

The first run found three eigenmodes at 1.176, 2.062, and 2.197 GHz. Compare these against the cutoffs. Port 4 has TM modes with cutoffs at 2.228 and 2.395 GHz, very close to eigenmodes 2 and 3. A loaded mode whose cutoff sits almost on top of an eigenfrequency has \(\sqrt{\omega^2-\omega_c^2}\) near zero, which makes the rational approximation poorly conditioned and contaminates the solution.

docs.title: Rerun with only the propagating modes
docs.text:
Load exactly the modes that propagate at the eigenfrequencies of interest:

in2.omega3p
Port : {
  ReferenceNumber : 4
  NumberOfModes : 2
}
Port : {
  ReferenceNumber : 7
  NumberOfModes : 3
}
Mode in1 f (GHz) in1 Qext in2 f (GHz) in2 Qext 1 1.176 267 1.176 271 2 2.062 496 2.057 273 3 2.197 749 2.196 693

Mode 1 is unaffected since no cutoff is near it. Modes 2 and 3 change noticeably, and the second run is the trustworthy one. The lesson generalizes: load all propagating port modes and no evanescent mode whose cutoff is close to an eigenfrequency. Run once with many modes to learn the cutoffs, then run again with the right count.

Complex electric fields of the three modes from the second run.

docs.title: Pic3P
docs.text:
Pic3P is the electromagnetic particle-in-cell mode of the T3P time-domain solver. It advances Maxwell's equations and the particles together, so the fields the particles feel include their own space charge, image charges on the walls, and the wakefields they leave behind. It is the tool for RF guns and other low-energy, high-charge situations where the beam modifies the fields it moves in.

There is no separate pic3p executable. A .pic3p input file is run with t3p, and T3P switches to PIC mode when it finds a Loading block with Particles inside. Results go to t3p_results/.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
Question Tool Where do field-emitted or secondary electrons go in a given RF field?
