The heat loads at the intercepts are what the cryogenic designer needs: 0.6 mW at 2 K, 40 mW at 4 K, 0.78 W at 70 K, for one sixteenth of the coupler. The maximum temperature of 324 K is on the antenna tip, above ambient because of RF heating with no cooling path other than conduction.

Shell power is reported as zero

ResultFile lists P (SideSet 6) = 0 and P (SideSet 7) = 0. These are the shell surfaces, and the RF heat applied to them is accounted for through the shell elements rather than as a boundary flux, so it does not appear in the sideset power tally. The symmetry planes 10 and 11 show nonzero power, which indicates the shell heat is reported there instead. Treat the per-sideset numbers on shell runs with care.

docs.title: Tutorial 3: Lorentz force detuning of an SRF cell
docs.text:
Example directory: examples/tem3p/SRFCell

A 3 mm thick niobium cell from a TESLA cavity at 35 MV/m. Radiation pressure pushes the walls, the cell deforms, and the frequency shifts. This is an elastic-only TEM3P run; no thermal problem is involved.

Half-cell models. Vacuum mesh sidesets: 1 symmetry plane, 2 and 3 disk centers, 6 wall. Shell mesh: 1 symmetry, 2 and 3 disks, 4 outer wall, 5 inner wall.

docs.title: Omega3P
TEM3P
docs.text:
SRFCell.tem3p
ElasticProblem: {
  MeshFile: SRFCellShell.ncdf
  BasisOrder: 2
  CurvedSurfaces: on

  MeshDump: {
    WriteDeformedEMMesh: on
    EMMeshInputDir: omega3p_results
  }

  LinearSolver: { Solver: CG  Preconditioner: DIAGONAL  Tolerance: 1.00e-10  MaxIterations: 150000 }

  VolumeMaterial: {                       // niobium
    Id: 1
    ElasticLambda: 13.5386473e+10
    ElasticMu:      4.2736232e+10
    ElasticAlpha:   6.50000e-6
  }

  Boundary: { Id: 1  ConditionType: Mixed  MixedType: NEUMANN DIRICHLET NEUMANN  MixedValue: 0., 0., 0. }  // symmetry
  Boundary: { Id: 2  ConditionType: Dirichlet  DirichletValue: 0. }    // one disk fully fixed
  Boundary: { Id: 3  ConditionType: Neumann  NeumannValue: 0. }        // other disk free
  Boundary: { Id: 4  ConditionType: Neumann  NeumannValue: 0. }        // outer wall free

  Boundary: {
    Id: 5                                 // inner wall
    ConditionType: LFDetuning
    Directory: omega3p_results
    Omega3PId: 6                          // the wall is sideset 6 in the vacuum mesh
    WhichMode: 0
    Method: Gradient
    TargetGradient: 35e6
    StartPoint: 0.0, 0.0, -0.0577
    EndPoint:   0.0, 0.0,  0.0577
  }
}

Omega3PId: 6 is the essential link: the inner wall is sideset 5 in the shell mesh but sideset 6 in the vacuum mesh, and this key tells TEM3P which vacuum surface supplies the pressure. One disk is fully fixed and the other left free, which models a cell that can lengthen; a stiffer tuner would fix both.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
ResultFile
#  u_x min [m]   u_x max [m]   u_y min [m]   u_y max [m]   u_z min [m]   u_z max [m]   u_mag max [m]  block_id
  -1.813e-07     1.808e-07     -1.569e-07    1.808e-07     -1.942e-06    3.344e-08     1.947e-06      1

The wall moves by at most 1.9 μm, almost entirely in z, at the free disk. The Omega3P rerun on DeformedVacuumMesh.ncdf gives:

Frequency Undeformed 1,300,957,728.5 Hz Deformed 1,300,950,556.4 Hz Shift −7.17 kHz

A static Lorentz force detuning coefficient is the shift divided by the gradient squared: −7.17 kHz / (35 MV/m)² = −5.9 Hz/(MV/m)². Measured values for TESLA cavities with stiffening rings are around −1 Hz/(MV/m)² and for unstiffened cells several times larger, so this unstiffened single cell with one free end is in the expected range.

The π-mode electric field on the vacuum mesh, and the displacement on the shell mesh. The free disk at right moves outward; the iris at left is fixed.

docs.title: Tutorial 4: mechanical eigenmodes of a TESLA cavity
docs.text:
Example directory: examples/tem3p/TeslaCavity

Mechanical vibration modes of a nine-cell cavity can be driven by pumps or helium pressure fluctuations and modulate the RF frequency. This example computes the five lowest modes of a half cavity.

docs.title: Mesh
docs.text:
The CAD model has fifteen bodies: cells, irises, and end plates. The journal deletes the end plates, unites everything into one niobium volume, and uses a half model with the symmetry plane selected by coordinate. 286,556 elements.

TeslaCavity.jou (excerpt)
import acis "TeslaCavity.sat"
delete volume 14 15                         # end plates
unite volume 6 4 7 1 5 3 13 12 11 10 9 8 2
compress ids

group 'ss1' add surface 8                   # end plane
group 'ss2' add surface 100                 # end plane
group 'ss3' add surface with y_min > -0.1   # symmetry plane
group 'ss4' add surface all
ss4 subtract ss1 from ss4
ss4 subtract ss2 from ss4
ss4 subtract ss3 from ss4
Sideset 1 surface in ss1
Sideset 2 surface in ss2
Sideset 3 surface in ss3
Sideset 4 surface in ss4

block 1 volume 1
block 1 element type tetra10
volume 1 sizing function type skeleton scale 7 time_accuracy_level 2 min_size 2.5 max_size 15 max_gradient 2
mesh vol 1
transform mesh output scale 0.001
export genesis "TeslaCavity.gen" overwrite

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
TeslaCavity.tem3p
ElasticProblem: {
  MeshFile: TeslaCavity.ncdf
  BasisOrder: 2
  CurvedSurfaces: on

  MeshDump: {
    WriteDeformedMesh: on
    MeshDeformScale: 0.2          // exaggerate mode shapes in the output meshes
  }

  EigenSolver : {
    NumEigenvalues: 5
    FrequencyShift: 5             // Hz
  }

  VolumeMaterial: {               // niobium
    Id: 1
    ElasticLambda: 20.9512e+10
    ElasticMu:      5.77227e+10
    ElasticAlpha:   6.50000e-6
    Density: 8570                 // kg/m^3, required for eigenmodes
  }

  Boundary: { Id: 1  ConditionType: Dirichlet  DirichletValue: 0. }    // end fixed
  Boundary: { Id: 2  ConditionType: Dirichlet  DirichletValue: 0. }    // end fixed
  Boundary: { Id: 3  ConditionType: Mixed  MixedType: NEUMANN DIRICHLET NEUMANN  MixedValue: 0., 0., 0. }  // symmetry
  Boundary: { Id: 4  ConditionType: Neumann  NeumannValue: 0. }        // free
}

The presence of EigenSolver turns the static problem into an eigenproblem. Density is mandatory since the mass matrix needs it. Both ends are clamped. The half model with a y-symmetry plane captures the longitudinal modes and the transverse modes polarized in x; the y-polarized transverse modes are excluded by the symmetry.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
srun -n 16 tem3p TeslaCavity.tem3p tem3p_results

1.54 million DOFs at order 2. ResultFile:

   62.822941       -0.44492086   0.00016858    -0.00254990  0.00265115   -0.12532522   0.12523272   0.44516552     1

docs.title: Track3P
docs.text: Track3P tracks charged particles through the electromagnetic fields computed by Omega3P, S3P, or T3P. Its two main uses are multipacting analysis, where secondary electrons resonate with the RF field and multiply, and dark current analysis, where field-emitted electrons are accelerated through the structure. Both produce impact statistics, trajectories, and derived quantities such as resonant particle maps and enhancement counters.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Track3P loads a mesh and a field solution, launches primary particles from chosen surfaces, and integrates their motion under the Lorentz force. When a particle hits a wall, Track3P records the impact and, depending on the material assigned to that wall, either absorbs the particle or emits secondaries. Tracking continues for a specified number of RF cycles. A post-processing stage identifies particles whose trajectories repeat in phase with the RF, which is the signature of multipacting.

flowchart LR
    A["Cubit + acdtool<br/>mesh.ncdf"] --> C
    B["Omega3P / S3P<br/>field files"] --> C["Track3P<br/>launch, track, impact,<br/>secondary emission"]
    C --> D["resonantparticles<br/>enhancementCounter<br/>ImpactsInfo"]
    C --> E["partpath_ts*.ncdf<br/>trajectory animation"]
    D --> F["ParaView macros,<br/>acdtool postprocess track3p,<br/>your own scripts"]

Parallelization. Every MPI rank loads the entire mesh and field. Particles are divided evenly across ranks and tracked independently, so there is no inter-rank communication and load balance is nearly perfect. The cost is memory: each rank holds the full problem. Within a rank, the particle loop is OpenMP-parallel, so a hybrid run with few ranks and many threads is often the best use of a node. A cryomodule dark-current study with 1.5 million elements and 2 million particles over 50 RF cycles ran in about 7 minutes on 240 cores.

docs.title: Multipacting background
docs.text:
Electrons released from a cavity wall are accelerated by the RF field and strike another point on the wall. If the impact energy falls in the range where the secondary emission yield (SEY) exceeds one, more than one electron leaves for each that arrives. If, in addition, the trajectory returns in phase with the RF so that the process repeats, the population grows exponentially. That avalanche is multipacting, and it limits achievable gradient in cavities, couplers, and windows.

Multipacting is classified by order, the number of RF cycles a resonant electron takes to return to its launch site, and by points, the number of distinct impact sites in one period. Two-point multipacting between opposing walls at the equator of an elliptical cavity is the classic case.

Track3P separates the dynamics from the material. The tracking run finds trajectories that are resonant for the given geometry and field level, independent of surface condition. The enhancement counter then weighs each resonant trajectory by the SEY at each of its impact energies:

\[ \mathrm{EC} = \delta_1 \cdot \delta_2 \cdots \delta_m \]

where \(\delta_i\) is the SEY at the \(i\)-th impact. EC above one means the trajectory would grow for that surface; the larger EC, the harder the barrier. Because the SEY enters only at the post-processing stage, one tracking run can be evaluated against several surface treatments.

A resonant trajectory bouncing between two points near an iris, from a Track3P benchmark against measured barriers on the ICHIRO cavity.

docs.title: Input file
docs.text:
Every block and key is described in the Track3P command syntax.

The input <project>.track3p does not use the ModelInfo and FiniteElement blocks of the other solvers. The mesh and fields come from the solver results directory named in Domain. A complete multipacting scan:

Pillbox.track3p
FieldScales: {
  Type: FieldGradient        // FieldGradient | InputPortPower | StorEnergy
  ScanToken: 1               // 1 scan a range, 0 single level
  Minimum: 23.0e+6           // V/m
  Maximum: 25.0e+6
  Interval: 1.0e+6
}

NormalizedField: {           // defines "gradient" for FieldGradient scaling
  StartPoint: 0.0 0.0 -0.057
  EndPoint:   0.0 0.0  0.057
}

Domain: {
  FieldDir: ./omega3p_results
}

Emitter: {
  BoundaryID: 6              // emit from this surface
  x0: 0.03  x1: 0.035        // only within this bounding box
  y0: 0.04  y1: 0.1
  z0: -0.045 z1: 0.0
}

Material: { Type: Primary    BoundarySurfaceID: 6 }
Material: { Type: Secondary  BoundarySurfaceID: 6 }
Material: { Type: Absorber   BoundarySurfaceID: 1 2 }

OutputImpacts: on

Postprocess: {
  Toggle: on
  ResonantParticles: { Token: on }
  EnhancementCounter: {
    Token: on
    MinimumEC: 0.01
    SEYFileName1: copper.dat
    BoundarySurfaceID1: 6
  }
}

Every default is written out for you

Track3P writes InputParameters into the results directory with every block, every keyword, and every default value it used, annotated with comments. That file is the most complete reference for the input format. Read it after your first run.

docs.title: Top-level keywords
docs.text: Keyword Default Meaning TotalTime 20 Tracking duration in RF cycles OutputImpacts off Write every impact to ImpactsInfo_<level>. Needed for resonant-particle analysis and for Faraday-cup post-processing. ParticlesTrajectories Sub-block controlling trajectory output; only active when ScanToken is 0. Keys ParticleFile (prefix, default partpath), Start, Stop, Skip in time steps.

docs.title: FieldScales
docs.text:
Key Meaning Type FieldGradient scales to an average accelerating gradient in V/m over the line in NormalizedField. InputPortPower scales to watts at the input port of an S3P solution. StorEnergy scales to joules of stored energy. ScanToken 1 to scan from Minimum to Maximum in steps of Interval; 0 to run a single level given by Scale Minimum, Maximum, Interval Scan range, in the units of Type Scale Single field level when ScanToken is 0

Every scan point is a complete tracking run, so a 30-level scan costs 30 times a single level.

docs.title: NormalizedField
docs.text: Only used with Type: FieldGradient. StartPoint and EndPoint define the line along which the accelerating voltage is integrated, N the number of points (default 300), and Beta the particle velocity for the transit-time factor (default 1). Set the line to the cavity's active length so that "gradient" means what it does in RF test data.

docs.title: Domain
docs.text: Key Default Meaning FieldDir Omega3P or S3P results directory ModeID1 0 Which mode to load from FieldDir dt 1.0 Time step factor; the step is dt / frequency / 100 MaxImpacts 50 Particles are dropped after this many impacts LowEnergy, HighEnergy 5 eV, 1e9 eV Impacts outside this energy window kill the particle InitialEnergy 2 eV Launch energy of primaries Bins 64 Spatial binning used to locate particles in the mesh. Increase for large or elongated meshes; the Tesla example uses 640. ExternalMagneticField 0 0 0 Uniform external B in tesla MagneticFieldMap Sub-block loading a tabulated field: File, Scaling, Units, ZOffset ElectroStaticFieldMap Sub-block loading a static electric field on a Cartesian grid, as written by gun3pOutputConverter from a Gun3P run: File, Scaling. The RF field and the static field are summed at each particle position. SymmetryFactor, SymmetryPlane 1, none Symmetry of the model and the sideset of the symmetry plane, used with a SymmetryPlane material so that emitted current is scaled to the full structure SolidRegion, VacuumRegion Block IDs for dielectric and vacuum, needed when particles emit from or cross a dielectric surface as in windows Voltage 0 External DC voltage between two radii: a ra rb, giving V = a / log(rb / ra)

docs.title: Emitter
docs.text:
One block per emission region. Primaries launch from faces of BoundaryID whose centroids fall inside the box x0..x1, y0..y1, z0..z1. Defaults for the box are effectively infinite, so an Emitter with only BoundaryID uses the whole surface.

Type Name Use 2 ElectronicSurface Default. Uniform launch from a metal surface over RF phase for multipacting. 5 SolidElectronicSurface Launch from a dielectric surface, for windows. Requires SolidRegion in Domain. 7 FieldEmission Fowler-Nordheim emission for dark current. Takes N particles, WorkFunction in eV, and field enhancement Beta. 10 LoadParticles Read an initial particle set from a text file given as ParticlesFile: one line per particle with electron count, energy in eV, position, and momentum. Optional XScale, YScale, ZScale, EnergyScale, and XOffset, YOffset, ZOffset rescale and shift the file. Added in 2025.

Other types exist in the code (ThermalCathode, Injector, ChildLangmuir, and so on) but are not exercised by the tutorials. ChildLangmuir is the model Gun3P uses. Emission runs from t0 to t1 in RF cycles, default the first cycle only.

docs.title: Material
docs.text:
Assigns behavior to surfaces by sideset, or to dielectric volumes by SolidBlockID.

Type Behavior Primary Primaries may be launched here. Pair with an Emitter. Secondary Impacts here generate secondaries. Model: 1 (default) for multipacting; Model: 2 for dark current, which also accepts an inline SEY table via Sigma0 and Einit, plus MinimumNumElectrons and ElasticThreshold. Absorber Impacts here kill the particle. Use for ports and beam pipe ends. SymmetryPlane Particles reflect specularly. Use on symmetry planes of a half or quarter model together with Domain.SymmetryFactor and Domain.SymmetryPlane, so that the tracked population represents the full structure. Using Absorber on a symmetry plane instead silently loses every particle that crosses it.

A surface can appear in both a Primary and a Secondary block, as the cavity wall does in every example.

docs.title: Postprocess
docs.text:
Sub-block Keys Output ResonantParticles InitialImpacts (default 4), EnergyRange (default 10 to 10000 eV), PhaseTolerance (default 0.01) OUTPUT/resonantparticles and one OUTPUT/MPParticles<level> per field level EnhancementCounter MinimumEC, SEYFileName1, BoundarySurfaceID1, and optionally a second SEY file and surface OUTPUT/enhancementCounter FaradayCup BoundaryID list One OUTPUT/faradaycup_<id> per surface, recording every impact there. Dark current only.

The SEY file is two columns, impact energy in eV and yield, one pair per line. copper.dat in the example directories is the standard copper curve.

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
track3p <project>.track3p [results_dir]

The optional second argument names the results directory, default track3p_results. Use it to keep several runs on the same input side by side, as the examples do with 2.3MV, track3p_solid, track3p_3T.

Resource guidance differs from the field solvers. Because each rank holds the full mesh, start with few ranks and use OpenMP threads for the rest of the node:

export OMP_NUM_THREADS=16
srun -n 1 -c 16 track3p Pillbox.track3p

Add MPI ranks when the particle count is large enough that one rank's share takes too long, keeping total memory per node in mind.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Location Content track3p.log, track3p.warn Log and warnings. The log ends with the field scale factor applied at each level. InputParameters Every input keyword with the value used, including defaults ImpactsInfo_<level> Every impact at that field level, if OutputImpacts is on. Columns: initial particle ID and impact number, initial and impact positions, initial and impact RF phase, impact energy, electrons in the macroparticle, momentum, face and volume IDs. OUTPUT/resonantparticles All resonant impacts at all levels. Columns: field level, particle ID, impact position, impact energy, launch position, total time, impact count. This is the file behind the multipacting map. OUTPUT/enhancementCounter Per resonant particle: field level, ID, EC, average and maximum EC, and the impact counts they were taken at. Newer versions append the final impact location. OUTPUT/MPParticles<level> Full impact-by-impact history of each resonant particle at that level OUTPUT/faradaycup_<id> Impacts on a monitored surface, dark current runs PARTICLES/partpath_ts<step>.ncdf Particle positions at each saved time step, for animation. Written only for single-level runs. PARTICLES/emissionevents_ts<step>.ascii Emission events per step

docs.title: Post-processing
docs.text:
Three routes, in increasing order of effort:

  1. ParaView macros. Load the mesh and mode file through the SLAC toolbar, then use the resonant, enhancement, and trajectory macros from the local tools page. resonant plots impact energy against field level and marks impact locations on the model; enhancement plots EC against field level; the SLAC reader animates partpath_ts*.ncdf.
  2. acdtool. acdtool postprocess track3p <project>.acdtool [results_dir] recomputes the enhancement counter with a different SEY file, or extracts single-particle trajectories by ID as plain text. See Tutorial 1.
  3. Your own scripts. The output files are whitespace-separated tables with a header line. The S3DF workflow project includes a matplotlib script that produces the multipacting map and enhancement-counter chart shown in Tutorial 1 directly from OUTPUT/.

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text:
1. Pillbox cavity: multipacting scan: the complete workflow from Omega3P fields to the multipacting map, plus a single-level trajectory run and acdtool post-processing. Includes a 2026 rerun on S3DF.
  2. Window: emission from a dielectric: S3P traveling-wave fields, solid and vacuum emission types.
  3. Muon cooling cavity: external magnetic field: uniform and mapped external B fields.
  4. Tesla cavity: dark current: Fowler-Nordheim emission with and without secondaries, Faraday cup output.
  5. Traveling-wave structure: dark current from S3P fields: field emission in a 7-cell structure driven through ports, with a symmetry plane and copper secondary emission.
  6. Static plus RF fields: loading a Gun3P electrostatic field alongside an S3P field for a DC-biased coax.

docs.title: Track3P tutorials
docs.text: Six worked examples from examples/track3p. The first four are from the CW18 workshop; the last two were added for CW23 and exist only in the group copy of the examples at /sdf/group/rfar/ace3p/cw23/examples/track3p. Each requires a field solution first, so the Omega3P or S3P step is shown briefly and the Track3P step in full. Meshing and acdtool meshconvert are covered in the Omega3P pillbox tutorial.

docs.title: Tutorial 1: pillbox cavity multipacting scan
docs.text:
Example directory: examples/track3p/Pillbox

The same rounded pillbox as the Omega3P tutorials, here as a full 360 degree model rather than a quarter, scanned from 23 to 25 MV/m for multipacting.

docs.title: Step 1: Fields from Omega3P
Step 2: Multipacting scan
Step 3: Read the results
docs.text:
OUTPUT/resonantparticles has one row per resonant impact:

 Field_Level    ID    Resonant_X   Resonant_Y   Resonant_Z     Energy     Initial_X    Initial_Y    Initial_Z    Total_time    Total_Num
 2.30000e+07  16100  4.73236e-02  8.80929e-02  7.68720e-05  1.47562e+01  3.16915e-02  5.95758e-02 -4.32326e-02  1.98753e+01     39
 2.30000e+07  16100  4.71849e-02  8.81666e-02 -1.84656e-04  1.43454e+01  3.16915e-02  5.95758e-02 -4.32326e-02  1.98753e+01     39

Particle 16100 launched from (31.7, 59.6, -43.2) mm and is now bouncing across the equator at z near zero with about 15 eV per impact, having made 39 impacts in 19.9 RF cycles. That is a two-point, first-order trajectory. Hundreds of such rows per level make up the map.

OUTPUT/enhancementCounter weighs each resonant particle by the copper SEY:

  fieldlevel         ID      enhancement      averageEnhancement     maxEnhancement        maxEnhancementImpactNum   totalImpactNum
 2.30000e+07       2300      1.13300e+00          1.06442e+00          1.27139e+00                    1                    2

docs.title: The multipacting map
docs.text:
Plot impact energy against field level, either with the resonant ParaView macro or with a short script. The scan covers only three levels so the "map" is three columns, but the structure is clear: distinct bands of impact energy at each level corresponding to different trajectory families.

Left: the 2016 Track3P build used for the CW18 workshop. Right: the same input rerun in July 2026 on S3DF with the current build, plotted with the workflow project's matplotlib script. Bars show resonant particle count per level.

The two runs agree on the qualitative picture but not on the numbers, and that is worth dwelling on. The 2016 run found resonant impacts up to 84 eV; the 2026 run tops out at 42 eV. Resonant particle counts dropped from 642, 518, 642 to 522, 392, 528 across the three levels. Ten years of development separate the two binaries, and the trajectory integrator, impact detection, and resonance criteria have all changed. Treat numbers in old tutorial material as illustrations of the method, not as reference values, and when a result matters, establish your own baseline with the build you are using.

Enhancement counter against field level. The 2016 run shows a spread of EC values per level reaching 1.4. The 2026 run, summarized as the maximum per level, stays below 1.0 everywhere.

The consequence of the lower impact energies in the newer run is visible in the enhancement counter. Copper's SEY crosses 1.0 near 300 eV, so impacts at 15 to 40 eV have SEY of about 0.1 to 0.3 and the product over many impacts is small. The newer build predicts no sustained multipacting for copper in this range; the older build predicted a soft barrier. Resolving which is right requires comparison against measurement, which is why the ICHIRO benchmark on the module page matters.

The resonant macro also marks impact sites on the model. They cluster on the equator, as expected for two-point multipacting in a pillbox.

docs.title: Step 4: Trajectories at one field level
docs.text:
To see what the particles are doing, rerun at a single level with trajectory output. Pillbox2.3MV.track3p differs from the scan input only in the FieldScales block:

FieldScales: {
  Type: FieldGradient
  ScanToken: 0
  Scale: 23.00e+6
  EmissionOutput: 1
}
TotalTime: 5

Give the run its own results directory so it does not overwrite the scan:

srun -n 1 -c 16 track3p Pillbox2.3MV.track3p 2.3MV

This writes 2.3MV/PARTICLES/partpath_ts*.ncdf, one file per time step. In ParaView, load mesh, mode file, and the particle file series through the SLAC toolbar, then press Play.

Two particles tracked from the wall to the equator, where they settle into tight two-point orbits.

docs.title: Step 5: acdtool post-processing
docs.text:
acdtool postprocess track3p recomputes the enhancement counter from the impact data with a different SEY file, so one tracking run can be evaluated for several surfaces, and extracts individual trajectories as text:

Pillbox.acdtool
EnhancementCounter: {
   Token               : on
   SEYFileName1        : copper.dat
   SEYFileName2        : copper.dat
   BoundarySurfaceID1  : 6
   BoundarySurfaceID2  : 6
   SolidVolID          : 0
   MinimumEC           : 0.01
   OutputFile          : en
}
Trajectory: {
   Token               : on
   ParticleID          : 16100 15400
}

srun -n 1 acdtool postprocess track3p Pillbox.acdtool 2.3MV

The enhancement counter goes to 2.3MV/en. Each trajectory goes to a file named by particle ID in the working directory, as rows of step number and position, ready for any plotting tool or for the trajectory ParaView macro.

docs.title: Tutorial 2: RF window with dielectric emission
docs.text:
Example directory: examples/track3p/Window

The alumina window from the S3P tutorials, now checked for multipacting. Windows are a classic multipacting site because electrons can be emitted from the ceramic surface as well as the metal, and because the traveling-wave field pattern differs from a standing wave.

docs.title: Fields from S3P
docs.text: S3P is run at the single operating frequency, 2.856 GHz, with the same input as the S3P window tutorial except Start equals End. The result is s3p_results/s3p.port7.mode0.f2.856000000E+09.mod, the field for excitation from port 7.

docs.title: Three emission configurations
docs.text:
The example has three input files that differ only in the Emitter blocks. The one that emits from both regions:

Window-Solid+VacuumEmission.track3p
TotalTime: 2

FieldScales: {
  Type: InputPortPower       // S3P field: scale by input power
  ScanToken: 0
  Scale: 8.0e+06             // 8 MW
}

Emitter: {                   // from the ceramic surface
  Type: 5
  x0: 0.0  x1: 0.045
  y0: 0.0  y1: 0.045
  z0: -0.002  z1: 0.0
  BoundaryID: 6
}

Emitter: {                   // from the metal wall
  Type: 2
  x0: 0.001  x1: 0.045
  y0: 0.001  y1: 0.045
  z0: 0.0    z1: 0.06
  BoundaryID: 6
}

Material: { Type: Primary    BoundarySurfaceID: 6 }
Material: { Type: Primary    SolidBlockID: 2 }
Material: { Type: Absorber   BoundarySurfaceID: 1 2 7 8 }
Material: { Type: Secondary  BoundarySurfaceID: 6 }
Material: { Type: Secondary  SolidBlockID: 2 }

Domain: {
  Bins: 128
  SolidRegion: 2             // ceramic block
  VacuumRegion: 1
  FieldDir: ./s3p_results
}

OutputImpacts: off

Three things are new here:

  • InputPortPower scaling. With an S3P field, "field level" is naturally the drive power. Scale: 8.0e+06 is 8 MW incident at port 7.
  • Emitter Type: 5 for the dielectric surface. The emitter box z0: -0.002, z1: 0.0 selects the ceramic face. Domain must declare which block is SolidRegion and which is VacuumRegion so Track3P knows which side of the surface is inside the dielectric.
  • Material blocks keyed by SolidBlockID rather than by boundary surface, assigning primary and secondary emission to the ceramic volume's surfaces.

Run each configuration into its own directory:

srun -n 1 -c 16 track3p Window-SolidEmission.track3p track3p_solid
srun -n 1 -c 16 track3p Window-VacuumEmission.track3p track3p_vacuum
srun -n 1 -c 16 track3p Window-Solid+VacuumEmission.track3p track3p_solid_vacuum

With ScanToken: 0, each run writes PARTICLES/partpath_ts*.ncdf for animation. The example directories include the resulting movies.

Particles emitted from the ceramic face (dense column at center) and from the metal walls (scattered points), in the traveling-wave field at 8 MW.

docs.title: Tutorial 3: external magnetic field
docs.text:
Example directory: examples/track3p/Muon201MHz

A 201 MHz cavity for muon ionization cooling operates inside a solenoid. The magnetic field bends electron trajectories and changes which ones are resonant, so multipacting must be evaluated with the external field present. Track3P accepts either a uniform field or a tabulated map.

The Omega3P input for this cavity has two features not seen earlier: two surface materials with different conductivity, since the end walls (sidesets 3 and 4) are beryllium windows rather than copper, and waveguide boundaries on the coupler ports (7 and 8).

docs.title: Three runs
docs.text:
The three input files share everything except the Domain block:

Muon.track3p (shared part)
TotalTime: 50

FieldScales: {
  Type: FieldGradient
  ScanToken: 1
  Minimum:  1.0e6
  Maximum:  16.0e6
  Interval: 1.0e6
}

NormalizedField: {
  StartPoint: 0.0 0.0 -0.18032
  EndPoint:   0.0 0.0  0.23657
  Beta: 1.0
}

Emitter: {
  x0: 0.4   x1: 0.65
  y0: 0.0   y1: 1.136
  z0: -0.25 z1: 0.25
  BoundaryID: 6
}

Material: { Type: Primary    BoundarySurfaceID: 6 }
Material: { Type: Secondary  BoundarySurfaceID: 3 4 6 }
Material: { Type: Absorber   BoundarySurfaceID: 7 8 }

OutputImpacts: on

Postprocess: {
  Toggle: on
  ResonantParticles: {
    InitialImpacts: 2
    EnergyRange: 50 3000
    Token: on
  }
}

A 16-level scan over 50 RF cycles each is a substantial run; use several MPI ranks. The Domain block for each case:

No external fieldUniform 3 T solenoidField map from a solenoid model 
Domain: {
  Bins: 256
  LowEnergy: 50
  HighEnergy: 3000
  FieldDir: ./omega3p_results
}

Domain: {
  Bins: 256
  LowEnergy: 50
  HighEnergy: 3000
  FieldDir: ./omega3p_results
  ExternalMagneticField: 0.0 0.0 3.0      // tesla
}

Domain: {
  Bins: 256
  LowEnergy: 50
  HighEnergy: 3000
  FieldDir: ./omega3p_results
  MagneticFieldMap: {
    File: BField
    // Scaling: 0.0001     // if the file is in gauss
    // Units: 0.001        // if coordinates are in mm
    ZOffset: 0.27          // shift the map's z origin
  }
}

The LowEnergy and HighEnergy cutoffs are raised to 50 eV and 3 keV here, and EnergyRange in ResonantParticles matches them. Low-energy impacts below the SEY crossover are not interesting for this cavity and dropping them early saves time.

docs.title: Compare the maps
docs.text:
Impact energy versus gradient without external field (left) and in a uniform 3 T solenoid field (right). Note the very different energy scales.

Without the magnetic field, resonant particles appear only at 1 and 2 MV/m with impact energies up to about 470 eV. With 3 T, they appear across the whole scan up to 12 MV/m, with impact energies of 1 to 2 keV, well into the range where copper's SEY exceeds one. The solenoid field confines electrons to tight helices along field lines, which makes resonance far easier to satisfy. This is the known multipacting problem of cooling-channel cavities, and the example reproduces it.

Resonant impact sites on the cavity, no external field. Sites cluster around the beryllium window and the coupler iris.

The example directory contains the corresponding plots for all three cases as RF-N, RF-3T, RF-M (impact energy) and RL-N, RL-3T, RL-M (locations).

docs.title: Tutorial 4: dark current in a Tesla cavity
docs.text:
Example directory: examples/track3p/Tesla

Dark current is field-emitted electrons from high-field regions of the wall, accelerated through the cavity and lost downstream or on the walls. Track3P models the emission with the Fowler-Nordheim law and, optionally, secondary emission at impacts.

docs.title: Fowler-Nordheim emission
docs.text:
The current density from a metal surface with work function \(\phi\) in eV under a field \(E\) enhanced by a geometric factor \(\beta\) is

\[ J = 1.54\times10^{-6}\,\frac{(\beta E)^2}{\phi}\,10^{4.52/\sqrt{\phi}}\, \exp\!\left(-\frac{6.53\times10^{9}\,\phi^{1.5}}{\beta E}\right) \]

Track3P converts \(J\) into a number of electrons per emitting face per time step. Typical \(\beta\) for a real cavity surface is 50 to 200; the example uses 120 with the copper work function.

docs.title: Primary emission only
With secondary emission and Faraday cups
docs.text:
Tesla-SEmission.track3p adds a dark-current secondary model and surface monitors:

Material: {
  Type: Secondary
  BoundarySurfaceID: 6
  Model: 2                   // dark-current secondary emission
  // inline SEY table for niobium
  Sigma0: 0.0 0.972 1.13 1.222 1.439 1.478 1.486 1.442 1.378 1.314 1.258 1.214 1.167 1.125 1.092 1.061 1.033 1.011 0.986 0.967 0.944 0.931 0.5
  Einit:  0.0 50 75 100 200 300 400 500 600 700 800 900 1000 1100 1200 1300 1400 1500 1600 1700 1800 1900 1e12
  MinimumNumElectrons: 1000
  ElasticThreshold: 1000
}

Postprocess: {
  Toggle: on
  ResonantParticles: { Token: off }
  FaradayCup: {
    Token: on
    BoundaryID: 6 1 2
  }
}

Model: 2 enables the dark-current secondary model: true secondaries following a Lye-Dekker yield curve given inline by Sigma0 against Einit, plus elastic reflection when a macroparticle carries more than ElasticThreshold electrons. MinimumNumElectrons prunes macroparticles that have shrunk below that count.

The FaradayCup post-processor writes every impact on each listed surface to OUTPUT/faradaycup_<id>, in the same column format as ImpactsInfo. Surfaces 1 and 2 are the beam pipe ends, so faradaycup_1 and faradaycup_2 are the dark current leaving the cavity upstream and downstream, which is what a real Faraday cup would measure. These files are the input to X-ray and radiation estimates.

Particles emitted from the first cell at 16 MV/m, tracked through the 9-cell Tesla cavity with secondary emission on. The white cluster at left is the emission site; particles that reach the far end are captured in the Faraday cup output.

docs.title: Scaling up: a cryomodule
docs.text:
The same input pattern extends to an entire LCLS-II cryomodule of eight 9-cell cavities, 10.96 m long, with 1.5 million particles emitted on the first RF cycle and tracked for 50 cycles. The mesh is refined at the irises, and a convergence check between 303 thousand and 1.45 million elements confirms the dark current loss map.

Pi-mode field at 1.2999669 GHz across one cavity of the cryomodule, and a snapshot of dark current particles tracked through it.

A run of this size is where the Track3P parallel model pays off: with no inter-rank communication it scales linearly in particles, and the 7-minute figure quoted on the module page is for this class of problem.

docs.title: Tutorial 5: dark current in a traveling-wave structure
docs.text:
Example directory: examples/track3p/TW7Cell (CW23 group copy)

A 7-cell S-band traveling-wave structure with input and output couplers. Unlike the standing-wave Tesla cavity, the field here comes from an S3P run at the operating frequency, and the structure is a half model, which introduces the symmetry-plane material.

docs.title: Fields from S3P
Track3P input
Results
docs.text:
srun -n 16 track3p TW7Cell-PEmission.track3p track3p_PEmission

The Faraday cup files record where the dark current goes:

Surface Primary emission only With copper secondaries 3, upstream pipe end 146 impacts 22,944 4, downstream pipe end 9 28,173 6, structure wall 35,450 2,336,484

With primaries alone, almost everything emitted from the iris lands back on the wall within the same cell or the next. Turning on the copper secondary-emission model (Model: 2 with the copper Sigma0 and Einit table, in TW7Cell-SEmission.track3p) multiplies the impacts on the wall by 66 and the current reaching the beam-pipe ends by over a hundred, because each wall impact spawns secondaries that are accelerated onward. The two runs bracket the real dark current; the surface condition decides where between them the structure sits.

Particles with secondary emission on, concentrated in the second and third cells downstream of the emission site.

The SEmission input also lowers MinimumNumElectrons and ElasticThreshold to 10, from 1000 in the Tesla example, so that macroparticles carrying fewer electrons survive; with N: 10 electrons per emitted macroparticle the Tesla thresholds would prune everything immediately.

docs.title: Tutorial 6: combining a static field from Gun3P
docs.text:
Example directory: examples/track3p/Coax-StaticField (CW23 group copy)

A coaxial line with a dielectric section, carrying both an RF wave from S3P and a DC bias computed by Gun3P. Track3P can superimpose the two.

Particles emitted from the coax walls and the dielectric surface, tracked in the RF plus static field. The dielectric section is at center.

docs.title: Three solvers
docs.text:
1. S3P on Coax-s3p.ncdf for the RF field at the drive frequency.
  2. Gun3P on Coax-gun3p.ncdf as a pure electrostatic solver, with MaxIterations: 0 so no particles are emitted, and ElectrostaticFieldToken: On in Outputs with a FileName and Nx, Ny, Nz. Then gun3pOutputConverter Coax-gun3p.in e writes the field on that Cartesian grid to gun3p_results/OUTPUT/E/test-101.txt.
  3. Track3P reads both:
Coax-track3p.in (excerpt)
FieldScales: {
  Type: InputPortPower
  ScanToken: 0
  Scale: 5                     // W
}

Domain: {
  FieldDir: ./s3p_results
  SolidRegion: 2
  VacuumRegion: 1
  ElectroStaticFieldMap: {
    File: ./gun3p_results/OUTPUT/E/test-101.txt
    Scaling: 1.0
  }
}

Emitter: { Type: 2  BoundaryID: 5 6  ... }     // metal walls
Emitter: { Type: 5  BoundaryID: 5 6  ... }     // dielectric surface

ElectroStaticFieldMap.File is the converter's text output and Scaling multiplies it, so one Gun3P solve at a reference voltage serves a scan of bias values. Note the key is spelled ElectroStaticFieldMap with a capital S inside, as the source reads it. The grid file is interpolated trilinearly onto particle positions and added to the RF field at every step.

This is the pattern for any device with a DC bias on an RF structure: a biased window, a DC-suppressed multipacting coupler, or an electron gun with an RF buncher.

docs.title: Keyword tables
docs.text:
These pages list the input-file keywords that each ACE3P module reads. They are generated from the source code, not written by hand. Keyword names, types, and default values therefore always match the release the documentation is built for. Use them to check spelling and defaults, and to find keywords the command syntax pages do not mention.

Page Covers Omega3P keywords Everything read in the omega3p/ source tree: eigensolver selection, frequency targets, adaptive mesh refinement, matrix output Shared EM keywords The emfem/ library used by all electromagnetic solvers: ModelInfo, boundary conditions, materials, coatings, FiniteElement Eigensolver keywords The solver/ library: Arnoldi, Lanczos, ESIL, CORK and SOAR nonlinear solvers, linear solver and preconditioner options

docs.title: How to read the tables
docs.text:
Column Meaning Keyword The name as it appears in the input file. Grouped under the block that contains it when the code reads a dotted path such as EigenSolver.SolverMode. Type int, double, string, or blank when the code reads the value into a pre-typed variable Default The value used when the keyword is absent. Blank means the code checks for presence with find() and handles absence in its own logic, or the entry is a block name rather than a scalar. Presence optional when a default exists; required when the solver aborts without it Read in Source file and line number, for developers tracing behavior

The tables are deliberately terse. Explanations of what each keyword does belong in the module guides, which link back here.

docs.title: How the pages are generated
docs.text:
ACE3P solvers read input through one uniform call:

const int nev = Get(kvc, "NumEigenvalues", InitOrFallback<int>(1) or quiet);

The script tools/extract_keywords.py in this repository scans the source for such calls, extracts the keyword, type, default, and severity, and writes these Markdown pages. It runs in continuous integration whenever an ACE3P release is tagged. See Contributing.

Coverage

Modules whose parsing uses a different pattern, notably T3P and Pic3P, are not yet covered by the extractor. Their keywords will be added as the script learns those patterns.

docs.title: acdtool command syntax
docs.text:
acdtool is the pre- and post-processing utility shared by all ACE3P modules. It has three groups of tasks:

Group Tasks meshconvert, meshconvertdirect Cubit Genesis to ACE3P NetCDF, with statistics and checks mesh stats, check, fix, deform, warpsurface, and others postprocess rf, eigentomode, volmontomode, wake_new, wake_direct, transwake, coaxsignal, pic3pstats, pic3pconvert, track3p, project resource Slurm resource guidance

All run serially except postprocess rf and postprocess volmontomode, which can use several ranks. Every invocation writes acdtool.log in the working directory and overwrites any previous one.

docs.title: meshconvert
docs.text:
acdtool meshconvert <mesh.gen> [out.ncdf]
acdtool meshconvertdirect <mesh.gen> [out.ncdf]

Converts the Genesis mesh from Cubit to NetCDF, prints the statistics of mesh stats, runs mesh check, and, for meshconvert, repairs inverted second-order tetrahedra by straightening their edges. meshconvertdirect converts without the repair. The output defaults to the input name with .ncdf. How to read the statistics is on the mesh preparation page.

docs.title: mesh
docs.text:
acdtool mesh stats  <mesh.ncdf>                  # statistics only
acdtool mesh check  <mesh.ncdf>                  # find inverted quadratic tets
acdtool mesh fix    <in.ncdf> <out.ncdf>         # straighten their edges
acdtool mesh deform <in.ncdf> <out.ncdf> <scale> # scale a TEM3P deformed mesh for viewing
acdtool mesh warpsurface <warp.in>               # export boundary triangles for the Warp code

warpsurface reads a small input file:

File: SNS_1Cell_Closed_12K.ncdf
ExteriorBoundary: 6
WarpFile: SNS_1Cell_Closed_12K.txt

and writes the triangles of that sideset as index (v1) (v2) (v3) for constructing a metal surface in Warp.

The source also contains boundary, merge, partition, pick, rotate, scale, shuntimpedence, smooth, straighten, summodes, surfsmooth, transform, untangle, and warp, which the command reference does not describe.

docs.title: resource
docs.text:
acdtool resource <input.omega3p>

Reads an Omega3P input, estimates the problem size, and writes a Slurm batch script with a node and core count for Perlmutter. The guidance it encodes, from the 2025 release notes:

Elements (M) DOFs (M) Nodes Cores/node Time under 1 under 6 1 64 under 30 min 1 to 2 6 to 13 2 64 under 30 min 2 to 4 13 to 25 4 32 under 30 min 4 to 5 25 to 32 6 32 under 30 min 5 to 6 32 to 38 10 8 under 60 min 6 to 7 38 to 44 20 8 under 60 min

This is for Omega3P with the MUMPS direct solver at order 2. Fewer cores per node on the larger problems reflects memory per rank as the limit.

docs.title: postprocess rf
docs.text:
acdtool postprocess rf <input.rfpost>
acdtool postprocess rf                 # writes sample.rfpost with every function

Computes RF quantities from an Omega3P or S3P mode. The input is a sequence of blocks; RFField must come first and every other block is a function enabled with ionoff = 1. The Omega3P post-processing page walks through a typical file; this section lists every function.

docs.title: RFField
docs.text:
RFField {
   ResultDir   = omega3p_results
   FreqScanID  = 0            // S3P only: scan point
   ModeID      = 0
   xsymmetry   = none         // none, electric, magnetic
   ysymmetry   = none
   gradient    = 2.00000e+07  // V/m; -1 for no scaling
   cavityBeta  = 1.00000
   reversePowerFlow = 0       // 1 charging, 0 decaying, for open ports
   x0 = 0.0  y0 = 0.0         // gradient integration line
   gz1 = -0.035  gz2 = 0.035
   npoint = 300
   fmnx = 10  fmny = 10  fmnz = 50   // localizer grid for tracking functions
}

ModeID for Omega3P is the eigenmode index; for S3P it indexes the port modes in the order the ports appear in the input. gz1 or gz2 above 10⁶ means the domain limit. xsymmetry and ysymmetry restore full-cavity stored energy for a symmetric model.

docs.title: Functions
docs.text:
All take ionoff. Coordinates in m; a coordinate above 10⁶ means the domain limit. modeID1 = modeID2 = -1 means all modes. Functions marked "RFField mode only" act on the single mode selected in RFField.
